regions.nuts1_disagreement: NUTS-1 DE1 (Baden-Wuerttemberg) merges historic Baden with Wuerttemberg; split here on 1806-1952 statehood history and the Alemannic vs Swabian dialect boundary.
regions.name: Baden
regions.identity_basis: Historic Grand Duchy of Baden (1806-1918); Alemannic-Baden dialect continuum along the Upper Rhine; distinct from Swabian Wuerttemberg despite shared federal state since 1952.
regions.population_note: Eurostat 2023 regional estimate, sum of NUTS-2 DE12 (Karlsruhe) + DE13 (Freiburg)

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Karlsruhe (KIT research) and Freiburg (university, environmental-tech hub) both function as established regional cultural centers
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: automotive supply, software (SAP), specialty chemicals, viticulture/tourism
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: strong Badener regional identity (Alemannic-Baden dialect, 1806-1952 statehood) fully integrated within Baden-Wuerttemberg/Germany, no separatism

autarky.rationale: Rhine-valley agriculture (wine, market gardening) and KIT/university-linked health infrastructure support mid-range scores; energy remains import-dependent post-nuclear-phaseout despite Rhine hydro; clothing production is fully offshored.

rationales.water: Upper Rhine groundwater and Black Forest headwaters give ample supply.
rationales.food: Rhine-valley market gardening and Kaiserstuhl/Ortenau viticulture support mid-range self-sufficiency, though the region is a net food importer overall.
rationales.energy: Post-nuclear-phaseout (Fessenheim/Philippsburg closures) leaves the grid import-dependent despite Rhine hydro and growing solar.

pole.note: No single dominant city; Karlsruhe (administrative/research) and Freiburg (university/eco-tech) share regional weight.

parliament.name: Landtag von Baden-Wuerttemberg
parliament.note: Baden has had no separate parliament since the 1952 merger into Baden-Wuerttemberg; represented via the joint Stuttgart Landtag. Parliament-rule exception.

regions.nuts1_disagreement: NUTS-1 DE1 merges Wuerttemberg with Baden; split on Swabian vs Alemannic dialect and separate pre-1952 statehood.
regions.name: Wuerttemberg
regions.identity_basis: Historic Kingdom of Wuerttemberg (1806-1918); Swabian dialect and cultural identity distinct from Alemannic Baden; strong regional pride (Schwabenland).
regions.population_note: Eurostat 2023 regional estimate, sum of NUTS-2 DE11 (Stuttgart) + DE14 (Tuebingen)

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Stuttgart metro >2.8M, automotive/engineering capital
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: automotive OEM and supply, precision engineering, optics, university research
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: distinct Swabian identity within Baden-Wuerttemberg/Germany; no separatism

autarky.rationale: Stuttgart's tight, expensive housing market pulls shelter down; a dense autobahn/rail network and Stuttgart Airport give strong transportation self-sufficiency; energy stayed import-heavy after the Neckarwestheim nuclear closure.

rationales.water: Neckar and Danube headwaters plus Swabian Jura karst aquifers provide solid supply for the population density.
rationales.food: Intensive orchard/viticulture belts (Remstal) and market gardening are real but insufficient for a dense industrial population.
rationales.energy: Neckarwestheim's 2023 nuclear closure removed the region's main baseload source; wind/solar buildout has not fully offset it.

pole.note: Stuttgart dominates as automotive/engineering capital.

parliament.name: Landtag von Baden-Wuerttemberg
parliament.note: Same shared Stuttgart Landtag as Baden since 1952. Parliament-rule exception.

regions.nuts1_disagreement: NUTS-1 DE2 (Bayern) merges Franconia into Bavaria; split here on East Franconian dialect and historic non-Bavarian identity (per Wiesinger).
regions.name: Franconia
regions.identity_basis: East Franconian dialect area; historic Franconian Circle/Duchy annexed to Bavaria 1803-06; retains a distinct Franconian identity, cuisine and Protestant-Catholic mix separate from Altbayern.
regions.population_note: Eurostat 2023 regional estimate, sum of NUTS-2 DE24 (Oberfranken) + DE25 (Mittelfranken) + DE26 (Unterfranken)

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Nuremberg -- metro >1.3M, media/cultural institutions
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: automotive supply, electronics (Siemens), insurance (Nuernberger), sports goods (adidas/PUMA)
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: strong Franconian identity within Bavaria/Germany; no separatist movement

autarky.rationale: Diversified Mittelfranken/Unterfranken industry and Erlangen's medical cluster support mid-to-strong scores; wine-growing Main valley aids food; clothing is offshored like everywhere else.

rationales.water: Main-Franconian river network and Fichtelgebirge headwaters are ample.
rationales.food: Main-valley wine, Knoblauchsland market gardening (Nuremberg) and Steigerwald grain give above-average regional food production.
rationales.energy: Grid-dependent with modest wind/solar; no major domestic generation asset gives it more than a mid-tier score.

pole.note: Nuremberg is the largest hub but Wuerzburg/Bamberg retain real cultural-administrative weight.

parliament.name: Bayerischer Landtag
parliament.note: The Bavarian Landtag (Munich) has jurisdiction over all of Bavaria, not just this cultural sub-unit. Parliament-rule exception.

reach.target: wider Bavarian and southern-Thuringian dialect-contact borderlands
reach.note: Nuremberg's media/legal institutions draw secondary cultural weight from adjacent southern Thuringia.

regions.nuts1_disagreement: NUTS-1 DE2 merges Bavarian Swabia into Bavaria alongside Altbayern/Franconia; split out on the separate historic Swabian Circle identity.
regions.name: Bavarian Swabia
regions.identity_basis: Swabian-Bavarian dialect transition zone; historically part of the Swabian Circle and Free Imperial Cities (Augsburg), annexed to Bavaria in 1806; distinct from both Altbayern and Baden-Wuerttemberg's Swabia.
regions.population_note: Eurostat 2023 regional estimate, NUTS-2 DE27 (Schwaben)

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Augsburg -- third-largest Bavarian city, former Free Imperial City, Fraunhofer research presence
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: aerospace supply, mechanical engineering, Allgaeu tourism/dairy
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: Bavarian-Swabian identity distinct from Altbayern within Bavaria/Germany

autarky.rationale: Allgaeu dairy farming supports food; Augsburg's aerospace-supply base is diversified but mid-tier; peripheral position versus Munich limits healthcare/transportation scores slightly.

rationales.water: Lech and Danube tributaries plus Allgaeu Alpine catchments give strong supply.
rationales.food: Allgaeu dairy farming is a genuine surplus sector (cheese exports beyond the region).
rationales.energy: Lech hydropower stations contribute, but the aerospace/engineering economy is otherwise grid-import-dependent.

sources: regional dialectology of the Bavarian-Swabian transition zone

pole.note: Augsburg is the clear regional hub; Allgaeu towns are secondary.

parliament.name: Bayerischer Landtag
parliament.note: Bavarian Landtag jurisdiction, not separate. Parliament-rule exception.

regions.nuts1_disagreement: NUTS-1 DE2 groups Altbayern/Munich with Franconia and Swabia under one Land; split here preserves Bairisch-dialect Altbayern as historically and dialectally distinct core.
regions.name: Munich / Altbayern
regions.identity_basis: Altbayern (Old Bavaria) -- historic core of the Wittelsbach Duchy/Kingdom of Bavaria; Bavarian (Bairisch) dialect and Catholic-Bavarian cultural identity, encompassing metropolitan Munich and its rural hinterland.
regions.population_note: Eurostat 2023 regional estimate, sum of NUTS-2 DE21 (Oberbayern) + DE22 (Niederbayern) + DE23 (Oberpfalz)

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Munich metro >6M, financial/cultural capital of Bavaria
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: automotive OEM, aerospace/defense, finance, biotech
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: strong Bavarian (Altbayern) identity within Germany; occasional autonomy rhetoric (Bayernpartei) but no active separatism

autarky.rationale: Alpine-fed Isar/Inn rivers give strong water security; Munich's extremely tight housing market drags shelter down; the Munich airport/autobahn hub and major hospital/biotech cluster push transportation and healthcare to the top of the scale.

rationales.water: Alpine-fed Isar/Inn rivers give near-maximal supply security.
rationales.food: Munich's Gaeuboden/Hallertau hinterland (Europe's largest hop-growing region) is a real agricultural surplus, though the metro population outstrips it.
rationales.energy: Isar hydropower plus grid imports; no single dominant domestic source keeps this mid-tier despite the wealth of the region.

pole.note: Munich dominates Altbayern as financial, cultural and political capital of Bavaria.

parliament.name: Bayerischer Landtag
parliament.note: The Bayerischer Landtag sits in Munich and governs the whole of Bavaria (incl. Franconia and Bavarian Swabia), not only Altbayern; the Land-level parliament does not map 1:1 onto this cultural unit. Parliament-rule exception, listed for the audit.

reach.target: Bavarian Swabia, western Austria (Tyrol/Salzburg), South Tyrol
reach.note: Munich functions as the primary metropolitan, financial and cultural draw well beyond its own administrative region, reaching into adjacent Alpine Austria and South Tyrol via Euregio-linked commuting, media market and hospital referrals.

regions.name: Hamburg
regions.identity_basis: Free and Hanseatic City of Hamburg; sovereign city-state since the medieval Hanseatic League; distinct maritime/mercantile identity and Low German (Hamburgisch) heritage.
regions.population_note: Eurostat 2023 estimate, Land of Hamburg (NUTS-2 DE60)

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Hamburg -- Germany's largest port, major media/publishing hub
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: maritime logistics, aerospace, media, trade finance
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: distinct Hanseatic city-state identity, fully integrated as a Land of Germany

autarky.rationale: A port city with strong logistics self-sufficiency but structurally food-import-dependent (no agricultural hinterland) and housing-constrained; the energy grid is supplemented by imports despite offshore-wind feed-in.

rationales.water: Elbe-fed groundwater is abundant for the city-state's footprint.
rationales.food: No agricultural hinterland within city-state borders; structurally import-dependent via the port.
rationales.energy: Offshore-wind feed-in helps, but port/industrial demand keeps the city a net importer.

pole.note: Single dominant city-state.

parliament.name: Hamburgische Buergerschaft
parliament.note: Hamburg is a sovereign city-state Land with its own parliament.

regions.name: Bremen
regions.identity_basis: Free Hanseatic City of Bremen, Germany's smallest Land; independent Hanseatic maritime identity distinct from surrounding Lower Saxony.
regions.population_note: Eurostat 2023 estimate, Land of Bremen (NUTS-2 DE50)

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Bremen/Bremerhaven -- historic Hanseatic port city-state
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: aerospace, automotive, container shipping, fisheries
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: sovereign Hanseatic city-state identity as a Land of Germany

autarky.rationale: Bremerhaven's container port and fishing fleet give strong transportation self-sufficiency; the tiny territory has no agricultural base, keeping food low; aerospace and automotive give a diversified but import-linked energy/materials picture.

rationales.water: Weser-fed groundwater is sufficient for the small city-state territory.
rationales.food: No meaningful agricultural hinterland within the city-state; entirely import-dependent.
rationales.energy: Bremerhaven's offshore-wind service industry does not translate into local generation share; grid-import dependent.

pole.note: Single dominant city-state (Bremerhaven is a satellite port, not a rival pole).

parliament.name: Bremische Buergerschaft
parliament.note: Bremen is a sovereign city-state Land with its own parliament.

regions.name: Schleswig-Holstein
regions.identity_basis: Historic Duchies of Schleswig and Holstein; distinct Low German/North Frisian and Danish-minority (South Schleswig) cultural layer; maritime Baltic-North Sea identity separate from Hamburg/Lower Saxony.
regions.population_note: Eurostat 2023 estimate, Land of Schleswig-Holstein (NUTS-2 DEF0)

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Kiel -- state capital, naval/maritime hub, university
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: wind energy, shipbuilding, agriculture, coastal tourism
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: distinct Schleswig-Holstein identity (including the Danish minority in Schleswig) within Germany

autarky.rationale: A leading German wind-energy exporter drives a high energy score; a strong agricultural base supports food; a peripheral position outside the major rail/air corridors limits transportation.

rationales.water: Ample rainfall and North/Baltic Sea coastal aquifers.
rationales.food: Strong North German Plain agriculture makes the Land a net food exporter.
rationales.energy: Germany's leading per-capita wind-energy exporter (on- and offshore); regularly generates far more electricity than it consumes.

sources: Danish-minority and North Frisian cultural literature

pole.note: Kiel is the state capital and largest city; Luebeck/Flensburg are secondary.

parliament.name: Landtag von Schleswig-Holstein
parliament.note: Own Land parliament.

regions.nuts1_disagreement: Matches NUTS-1 DE9 exactly; noted here only to disambiguate from Sachsen (Saxony, DED) despite the near-homophone English names -- see the Lower-Saxony/Saxony nuance addressed in this file's methodology notes.
regions.name: Lower Saxony
regions.identity_basis: Historic Land of Lower Saxony (post-1946); Low German (Niedersaechsisch) dialect zone distinct from Saxony proper (Upper Saxon/East Central German); North Sea coast, Lueneburg Heath and Volkswagen-industrial identity.
regions.population_note: Eurostat 2023 regional estimate, sum of NUTS-2 DE91-DE94 (Braunschweig, Hannover, Lueneburg, Weser-Ems)

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Hannover -- state capital, trade-fair capital (Hannover Messe)
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: automotive (VW), agriculture, offshore wind, logistics
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: Low-German Niedersachsen identity within Germany; no separatism

autarky.rationale: One of Germany's largest agricultural producers, giving high food and water scores; North Sea gas fields and offshore wind support energy; the VW-centered industrial base is diversified but Wolfsburg's company-town character caps healthcare/shelter slightly.

rationales.water: North Sea coastal aquifers and the Weser/Aller/Leine river network are abundant.
rationales.food: One of Germany's largest agricultural producers (grain, potatoes, livestock); a genuine net exporter.
rationales.energy: North Sea gas fields (declining but active) plus a large offshore/onshore wind fleet keep the Land energy-strong.

pole.note: Hannover is the state capital and trade-fair hub, but Lower Saxony is genuinely multi-polar across four NUTS-2 sub-regions.

parliament.name: Landtag von Niedersachsen
parliament.note: Own Land parliament, seated in Hannover.

regions.name: Lower Saxony (West / Weser-Ems)
regions.identity_basis: Hypothetical split-view record for the bremen-lower-saxony variant set: the western/Frisian half of Lower Saxony (Weser-Ems NUTS-2 DE94: Oldenburg, Cloppenburg, East Frisia, Emsland, Osnabrueck, Ammerland, Grafschaft Bentheim), organized around Oldenburg as its historic ducal-capital urban core, oriented toward Bremen's economic orbit.
regions.population_note: Landesamt fuer Statistik Niedersachsen 2023 estimate, Weser-Ems (NUTS-2 DE94); one of two split-view halves of de-lower-saxony's total (8,010,000).
regions.nuts1_disagreement: Weser-Ems (DE94) also includes Osnabrueck and Grafschaft Bentheim beyond the three districts (Oldenburg, Cloppenburg, East Frisia) explicitly named in the split-view mandate; the committed geometry has no finer NUTS-3 breakdown of DE94 available at the same NUTS-2 level as the 'together' baseline, so the full Weser-Ems NUTS-2 code is used, urban core kept at Oldenburg per the mandate.

pole.note: Oldenburg is the historic ducal capital and largest city of this split view, though Osnabrueck is comparably sized within the wider Weser-Ems NUTS-2 code.

parliament.name: Landtag von Niedersachsen
parliament.note: Hypothetical split-view territory, not an actual administrative unit; the real Landtag Niedersachsen governs the whole Land.

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Oldenburg -- historic ducal capital, regional cultural/administrative hub
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: agriculture/livestock, shipbuilding/maritime, automotive supply, offshore-wind service ports
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: hypothetical variant-view framing for the bremen-lower-saxony toggle; the underlying population holds a genuine Frisian/Oldenburg-orbit identity distinct from Hannover

autarky.rationale: East Frisian/Oldenburg farmland and livestock give top-tier food production; North Sea coastal aquifers are abundant; offshore-wind service ports support energy despite the region's peripheral position for rail transportation.

rationales.water: North Sea coastal aquifers and the Ems/Weser network are abundant.
rationales.food: East Frisian and Oldenburger Muensterland livestock/dairy farming is a genuine agricultural surplus.
rationales.energy: Offshore-wind service ports (Emden, Wilhelmshaven) and onshore turbines keep the region energy-strong.

regions.name: Lower Saxony (East / Hannover)
regions.identity_basis: Hypothetical split-view record for the bremen-lower-saxony variant set: the eastern half of Lower Saxony (Hannover NUTS-2 DE92, Braunschweig NUTS-2 DE91, and Lueneburg NUTS-2 DE93, all lying east of the Bremen enclave), organized around Hannover as the state capital and largest urban core.
regions.population_note: Landesamt fuer Statistik Niedersachsen 2023 estimate, sum of Braunschweig (DE91) + Hannover (DE92) + Lueneburg (DE93); the other split-view half of de-lower-saxony's total (8,010,000), complementing de-lower-saxony-west's Weser-Ems total.
regions.nuts1_disagreement: Groups all three NUTS-2 units lying geographically east of the Bremen enclave (Braunschweig, Hannover, Lueneburg) under the 'east/Hannover' split-view label; Lueneburg is included here rather than left as a coverage gap so the two split-view halves sum exactly to de-lower-saxony's total codes (DE91-94).

pole.note: Hannover is the state capital and clearly dominant urban core of this split view.

parliament.name: Landtag von Niedersachsen
parliament.note: Hypothetical split-view territory, not an actual administrative unit; the real Landtag Niedersachsen governs the whole Land.

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Hannover -- state capital, trade-fair capital (Hannover Messe)
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: automotive (VW Wolfsburg), trade fairs, tourism, logistics
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: hypothetical variant-view framing for the bremen-lower-saxony toggle; the underlying population holds a genuine Hannover-orbit identity distinct from the Frisian west

autarky.rationale: Braunschweig/Hannover farmland gives good food security; the VW-centered industrial base and Hannover trade-fair infrastructure support transportation and diversified industry; energy remains mid-tier without a major domestic generation asset in this eastern half.

rationales.water: Aller/Leine river network and Lueneburg Heath aquifers are ample.
rationales.food: Broad Boerde-adjacent farmland around Braunschweig/Hildesheim gives solid food production.
rationales.energy: No major domestic generation asset in this eastern half; mid-tier, grid-dependent.

regions.name: Lower Saxony united (incl. Bremen)
regions.identity_basis: Hypothetical 'united' view for the bremen-lower-saxony variant set: shows the Bremen city-state enclave absorbed into its surrounding Lower Saxony territory, reflecting Bremen's historical origin as a Lower-Saxon Hanseatic city and its complete geographic enclosure by Lower Saxony, while the default map keeps Bremen as its own sovereign Land.
regions.population_note: Sum of de-bremen (684,000) and de-lower-saxony's total (8,010,000) 2023 estimates.
regions.nuts1_disagreement: Overrides Bremen's sovereign city-state status (NUTS-1 DE5) to model a hypothetical territorial-geography view in which the enclave is shown merged with its surrounding Land; the default map keeps de-bremen and de-lower-saxony as two constitutionally separate Laender.

pole.note: Hannover (state capital) and Bremen (historic Hanseatic port) form the two real poles of this hypothetical united territory.

parliament.name: Landtag von Niedersachsen + Bremische Buergerschaft
parliament.note: Hypothetical unified variant view; Bremen (own Buergerschaft) and Niedersachsen (own Landtag) remain constitutionally separate Laender.

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Hannover and Bremen both function as established urban hubs in this hypothetical merged territory
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: port/maritime logistics, automotive, aerospace, agriculture
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: hypothetical territorial-geography framing reflecting Bremen's historical Lower-Saxon origin and complete geographic enclosure; does not claim Bremen's sovereign city-state status is invalid

autarky.rationale: Combines Bremen's port/aerospace logistics strength with Lower Saxony's agricultural and North Sea energy base; averaging the two underlying records with Bremen's small population having limited weight.

rationales.water: Combines Weser/Aller/Leine river network abundance from both underlying records.
rationales.food: Lower Saxony's substantial agricultural surplus offsets Bremen's zero-agriculture city-state footprint.
rationales.energy: Bremerhaven's offshore-wind service industry plus Lower Saxony's North Sea gas/wind base keep this combined view energy-strong.

regions.nuts1_disagreement: Matches NUTS-1 DED exactly, but note: Leipzig is sometimes analyzed as culturally distinct from Dresden/Chemnitz (different historical allegiance, more Thuringian-adjacent) and an internal Dresden/Leipzig split was considered and not applied here to keep the zone's region count from growing further beyond the explicitly mandated splits.
regions.name: Saxony
regions.identity_basis: Historic Kingdom/Electorate of Saxony; East Central German (Upper Saxon) dialect; distinct baroque-Dresden and industrial-Leipzig/Chemnitz cultural identity, etymologically unrelated to Lower Saxony despite the shared English name.
regions.population_note: Statistisches Landesamt Sachsen 2023 estimate, Land of Sachsen (NUTS-2 DED2, DED4, DED5)

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Dresden -- state capital, baroque cultural capital, semiconductor R&D
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: semiconductors, automotive, trade fairs/publishing (Leipzig), textiles
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: strong Saxon (Saechsisch) identity within Germany; no separatism

autarky.rationale: Lignite legacy plus a growing renewables build-out keeps energy mid-high; the Silicon Saxony semiconductor cluster and strong rail links support transportation and industry diversification.

rationales.water: Elbe and Mulde river network plus Erzgebirge headwaters are adequate for the population.
rationales.food: Fertile Leipzig lowland farmland is real but modest relative to the urban population.
rationales.energy: Lusatian/Central German lignite legacy plus a fast-growing renewables build-out keep the Land above the German average.

pole.note: Dresden is the state capital and baroque cultural seat; Leipzig rivals it in population and economic/publishing weight -- a genuine two-pole structure, not a single dominant city.

parliament.name: Saechsischer Landtag
parliament.note: Own Land parliament, seated in Dresden.

regions.nuts1_disagreement: NUTS-1 DEA (Nordrhein-Westfalen) merges Rhineland with Westphalia; split here on Rhenish (Ripuarian/Catholic-Carnival) vs Westphalian (Low German, mixed confession) cultural identity, per the historic Prussian Rhine Province vs Province of Westphalia.
regions.name: Rhineland
regions.identity_basis: Rhenish (Rheinlaendisch) cultural identity -- Catholic, Ripuarian-Franconian dialect, Carnival tradition, historic Prussian Rhine Province distinct from Westphalia.
regions.population_note: Eurostat 2023 regional estimate, sum of NUTS-2 DEA1 (Duesseldorf) + DEA2 (Koeln)

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Cologne -- media/cultural capital, cathedral city; Duesseldorf -- state capital, fashion/finance
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: chemicals, media, finance, lignite energy
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: distinct Rhenish identity within North Rhine-Westphalia/Germany; no separatism

autarky.rationale: The Rhenish lignite coalfield (declining but still active) keeps energy above the NRW average; the Rhine port, autobahn/rail density and Cologne-Bonn airport give near-maximal transportation self-sufficiency; dense metro housing pressure caps shelter.

rationales.water: Rhine river and groundwater are abundant, though industrial demand is high.
rationales.food: Dense urban/industrial land use leaves little agricultural hinterland; structurally food-import-dependent.
rationales.energy: The Rhenish lignite coalfield (declining, phase-out by 2030) still keeps energy above the national urban average.

pole.note: Cologne is the larger cultural/media hub; Duesseldorf is the NRW state capital and finance/fashion center -- two genuinely competing poles.

parliament.name: Landtag Nordrhein-Westfalen
parliament.note: The NRW Landtag (Duesseldorf) governs all of North Rhine-Westphalia, not just the Rhineland cultural unit. Parliament-rule exception.

regions.nuts1_disagreement: NUTS-1 DEA merges Westphalia with Rhineland; split here on the Westphalian dialect and historic Prussian-province identity distinct from the Rhenish Rhineland.
regions.name: Westphalia
regions.identity_basis: Historic Province of Westphalia; Low German/Westphalian dialect zone; post-industrial Ruhr-East and agrarian Muensterland identity distinct from Rhenish Rhineland.
regions.population_note: Eurostat 2023 regional estimate, sum of NUTS-2 DEA3 (Muenster) + DEA4 (Detmold) + DEA5 (Arnsberg)

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Dortmund -- largest Westphalian city, post-industrial services/logistics hub
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: mechanical engineering, logistics, agriculture, insurance/IT
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: distinct Westphalian identity within North Rhine-Westphalia/Germany

autarky.rationale: Muensterland's strong agricultural base lifts food; the post-coal Ruhr-East transition leaves energy mid-tier; dense rail/autobahn network from the old industrial core keeps transportation solid.

rationales.water: Ruhr/Lippe/Ems river network is adequate; former mining-subsidence water management remains an active engineering task.
rationales.food: Muensterland's strong agricultural base (livestock, grain) makes the region a net food exporter overall.
rationales.energy: Post-coal transition; wind and biomass are growing but do not yet replace the historic Ruhr coal baseload.

pole.note: Dortmund is the largest city but Muenster (administrative/university) and Bielefeld (Ostwestfalen) are comparable regional poles.

parliament.name: Landtag Nordrhein-Westfalen
parliament.note: Shared NRW Landtag with the Rhineland unit. Parliament-rule exception.

regions.name: Hesse
regions.identity_basis: Historic Grand Duchy/People's State of Hesse; Central Hessian dialect zone; Frankfurt's role as a historic Free Imperial City and modern financial capital anchors a state identity distinct from neighboring Rhineland/Westphalia.
regions.population_note: Eurostat 2023 regional estimate, sum of NUTS-2 DE71 (Darmstadt) + DE72 (Giessen) + DE73 (Kassel)

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Frankfurt am Main -- Germany's financial capital, major international airport hub
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: finance, pharma/chemicals, logistics, automotive supply
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: Hessian identity within Germany; no separatism

autarky.rationale: Frankfurt/Rhein-Main housing pressure pulls shelter down; Frankfurt Airport and the autobahn/rail hub give near-maximal transportation; the pharma/chemicals cluster (Sanofi, Merck) drives a strong healthcare score.

rationales.water: Rhine-Main groundwater and Vogelsberg volcanic-highland springs are ample.
rationales.food: Wetterau and Rheingau agriculture/viticulture are real but modest against the dense Rhein-Main population.
rationales.energy: No major domestic generation asset; the financial-sector economy is grid-import-dependent.

pole.note: Frankfurt dominates as financial capital, despite Wiesbaden being the formal state capital.

parliament.name: Hessischer Landtag
parliament.note: Own Land parliament, seated in Wiesbaden.

regions.name: Rhineland-Palatinate
regions.identity_basis: Post-1946 French-zone-administered Land; Palatine/Moselle-Franconian dialect continuum, wine culture (Palatinate, Moselle), and cross-border ties to French Lorraine and Luxembourg -- split from Saarland in v0.1.2 per the parliament rule, since both are already separate Laender with their own Landtage.
regions.population_note: Statistisches Landesamt Rheinland-Pfalz 2023 estimate, Land Rheinland-Pfalz (NUTS-2 DEB1+DEB2+DEB3); split from the former combined de-rhineland-palatinate-saarland total (5,090,000).
regions.nuts1_disagreement: Matches NUTS-1 DEB exactly. Previously combined with Saarland in v0.1.0 for region-count parsimony despite both already being separate Laender with their own Landtage; split in draft_v0.1.2 to satisfy the parliament rule (own parliament -> own cultural unit).

pole.note: Mainz is the Land capital and biotech hub; Trier/Koblenz/Kaiserslautern remain genuine secondary poles across the Land's elongated territory.

parliament.name: Landtag Rheinland-Pfalz
parliament.note: Own Land parliament, seated in Mainz. Splitting this unit out of the former combined record resolves the v0.1.0 parliament-rule exception.

regions.name: Zurich
regions.identity_basis: Switzerland's largest city-canton; German-speaking Reformed-Protestant economic and financial capital, historically the core of the medieval Zuerich city-state within the Confederacy.
regions.population_note: Swiss Federal Statistical Office (BFS) 2023 estimate, Canton of Zuerich

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Zuerich -- Switzerland's largest city, a global financial center
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: banking/finance, insurance, technology (ETH Zuerich), life sciences
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: Zuerich cantonal identity within the Swiss Confederation; cantonal sovereignty is the constitutional norm, not separatism

autarky.rationale: Alpine-fed lake and river water is abundant; the extremely tight, expensive housing market keeps shelter low; Zuerich Airport and the national rail hub give near-maximal transportation; the hospital/life-sciences cluster gives top-tier healthcare.

rationales.water: Alpine-fed lake and river water is abundant.
rationales.food: Dense urban canton with limited farmland; structurally food-import-dependent.
rationales.energy: Grid- and import-dependent; no major domestic generation asset within canton borders.

sources: Bundesamt fuer Statistik (Swiss Federal Statistical Office)

pole.note: Zuerich dominates its canton and the wider Swiss economy.

parliament.name: Kantonsrat des Kantons Zuerich
parliament.note: Single-canton unit; own cantonal parliament.

reach.target: Suisse Romande labor-market edges (Vaud/Fribourg), southern Baden-Wuerttemberg
reach.note: Zuerich anchors Switzerland's largest metropolitan labor market with cross-cantonal and cross-border (DE) commuting reach.

regions.name: Basel
regions.identity_basis: Historic Basel city-state plus Aargau; a tri-national Rhine-border identity (Basel borders both Germany and France) anchoring Europe's leading pharmaceutical cluster.
regions.population_note: Swiss Federal Statistical Office (BFS) 2023 estimate, sum of Basel-Stadt + Basel-Landschaft + Aargau cantons

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Basel -- global pharmaceutical capital, tri-national Rhine hub
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: pharmaceuticals, chemicals, logistics, precision manufacturing
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: Basel/Aargau cantonal identities within the Confederation; strong cross-border (DE/FR) economic integration, no separatism

autarky.rationale: The Rhine port and EuroAirport Basel-Mulhouse-Freiburg give strong transportation; the Novartis/Roche pharma cluster gives a top-tier healthcare score; energy remains grid- and import-dependent.

rationales.water: The Rhine and Jura foothill aquifers give abundant supply.
rationales.food: Aargau farmland offsets Basel-Stadt's dense urban footprint, giving a mid-range regional score.
rationales.energy: Grid-import-dependent; the pharma/chemicals cluster is a large consumer rather than producer.

pole.note: Basel dominates the tri-cantonal grouping.

parliament.name: Grosser Rat Basel-Stadt / Landrat Basel-Landschaft / Grosser Rat Aargau
parliament.note: This unit groups three cantons; each has its own cantonal parliament. Parliament-rule exception, listed for the audit.

conflict_flags.description: Neuchatel and Jura (and parts of Fribourg) are francophone cantons statistically grouped into the German-plurality 'Espace Mittelland' macro-region; the Romandie/German-Swiss linguistic boundary (the Roestigraben) runs through this region rather than around it. Shown as an independently toggleable overlay.

regions.name: Bern-Mittelland
regions.identity_basis: Federal capital region (Bern) plus the German/French-mixed 'Espace Mittelland' -- includes bilingual Fribourg and francophone Neuchatel/Jura within a German-plurality macro-region; a genuine internal linguistic-frontier tension, flagged rather than resolved.
regions.population_note: Swiss Federal Statistical Office (BFS) 2023 estimate, sum of Bern + Fribourg + Solothurn + Neuchatel + Jura cantons

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Bern -- Swiss federal capital
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: federal administration, watchmaking, precision instruments, agriculture
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: Bernese/Mittelland cantonal identities within the Confederation; internal French/German linguistic frontier flagged, no separatism

autarky.rationale: Broad agricultural land across the Mittelland plateau supports food; Jura/Neuchatel watchmaking gives clothing a small precision-craft nudge above the national baseline; hydropower keeps energy solid.

rationales.water: Aare river network and Bernese Oberland Alpine headwaters are abundant.
rationales.food: Broad Mittelland-plateau agriculture gives one of the stronger food scores among Swiss macro-regions.
rationales.energy: Aare hydropower plants keep the region solidly energy-positive.

pole.note: Bern is the federal capital and dominant hub of the Espace Mittelland grouping.

parliament.name: Grosser Rat des Kantons Bern / Grand Conseil de Fribourg / Kantonsrat Solothurn / Grand Conseil de Neuchatel / Parlement de la Republique et Canton du Jura
parliament.note: This unit groups five cantons; each has its own cantonal parliament. Parliament-rule exception, listed for the audit.

reach.note: Bern's reach as federal capital is political/administrative rather than metropolitan-economic, distinct in kind from Zuerich's larger economic gravity.

regions.name: Romandie / Geneva-Lausanne
regions.identity_basis: French-speaking Romandie core (Region lemanique); an international-organization hub (Geneva) and Alpine Valais; a distinct Francophone-Swiss cultural identity.
regions.population_note: Swiss Federal Statistical Office (BFS) 2023 estimate, sum of Vaud + Valais + Geneve cantons

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Geneva -- global diplomatic and international-organization capital
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: diplomacy, private banking, watchmaking, Alpine tourism
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: Francophone Swiss (Romandie) identity within the Confederation; no separatism

autarky.rationale: Alpine Valais hydropower supports energy; Geneva/Lausanne's tight housing market caps shelter; the international-organization and private-banking cluster supports transportation and healthcare capacity well above the national baseline.

rationales.water: Lake Geneva and Valais Alpine glacial catchments are abundant.
rationales.food: Vaud vineyards and Valais orchard/vegetable farming give solid mid-range food production.
rationales.energy: Valais Alpine hydropower makes the region a net electricity exporter despite dense Geneva/Lausanne urban demand.

pole.note: Geneva (international organizations) and Lausanne (Olympic/university seat) form a genuine two-pole structure along Lake Geneva.

parliament.name: Grand Conseil de Geneve / Grand Conseil de Vaud / Grand Conseil du Valais
parliament.note: This unit groups three cantons; each has its own cantonal parliament. Parliament-rule exception, listed for the audit.

regions.name: Central & Eastern Switzerland
regions.identity_basis: Combines the founding cantons of the old Swiss Confederacy (Zentralschweiz: Lucerne, Uri, Schwyz, Obwalden, Nidwalden, Zug) with the remaining Ostschweiz textile/Alpine cantons (St. Gallen, Thurgau, Appenzell Ausserrhoden/Innerrhoden, Glarus, Graubuenden) into one broad macro-region, now with Schaffhausen split out as its own unit per the v0.1.2 historical-founding mandate.
regions.population_note: Swiss Federal Statistical Office (BFS) 2023 estimate, sum of the 12 remaining cantons of Zentralschweiz + Ostschweiz (former 2,028,000 total for 13 cantons, minus Schaffhausen's ~84,000).
regions.nuts1_disagreement: A deliberately broad combination of two historically distinct macro-regions per the zone-1 spec; the internal heterogeneity (Zug's finance-haven status, Graubuenden's trilingual Romansh-speaking Alpine identity) remains real and could justify future subdivision. v0.1.2 removes Schaffhausen (CH052) into its own unit per the historical-founding mandate; see the schaffhausen variant set for the alternative combined-with-Schaffhausen framing (ch-central-eastern-combined, default_visible false).

pole.note: Lucerne is the historic Confederacy founding-city anchor; St. Gallen, Chur and Zug are real secondary poles across this heterogeneous macro-region.

parliament.name: Kantonsraete of Luzern, Uri, Schwyz, Obwalden, Nidwalden, Zug, St. Gallen, Thurgau, Appenzell Ausserrhoden, Appenzell Innerrhoden, Glarus (Landsgemeinde), Graubuenden
parliament.note: This unit groups twelve cantons; each has its own cantonal parliament (Glarus retains a Landsgemeinde open-air assembly). Parliament-rule exception, listed for the audit.

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Lucerne -- historic Confederacy founding city, tourism/culture hub; St. Gallen -- textile-heritage university city
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: finance (Zug), textiles (St. Gallen), Alpine tourism (Graubuenden/Lucerne), precision manufacturing
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: diverse cantonal identities (including Romansh-speaking Graubuenden) within the Confederation; a genuinely heterogeneous macro-region, no separatism

autarky.rationale: Alpine headwaters across Graubuenden/Uri give strong water security; Gotthard-region and Alpine hydropower push energy to the top of the scale; the St. Gallen textile-design heritage nudges clothing above baseline; peripheral Alpine valleys outside the Zug-Zuerich corridor limit transportation.

rationales.water: Alpine headwaters across Graubuenden/Uri/Glarus give strong per-capita water security.
rationales.food: Alpine dairy and some Thurgau/St. Gallen lowland farming give a mid-range score, well short of self-sufficiency for the population.
rationales.energy: Gotthard-region and central-Alpine hydropower push energy to the top of the Swiss scale.

regions.name: Central & Eastern Switzerland (incl. Schaffhausen)
regions.identity_basis: Hypothetical variant view for the schaffhausen variant set's 'current' (within-Ostschweiz) option: the v0.1.0 framing that statistically bundled Schaffhausen into the broad Zentral-/Ostschweiz macro-region, kept available as a toggle rather than deleted outright.
key_industries: tourism (Graubuenden Alps, Lake Lucerne, Rhine Falls)
regions.population_note: Swiss Federal Statistical Office (BFS) 2023 estimate, sum of the 13 cantons of Zentralschweiz + Ostschweiz incl. Schaffhausen (the v0.1.0 ch-central-eastern total).
regions.nuts1_disagreement: Reproduces the v0.1.0 ch-central-eastern grouping (13 cantons incl. Schaffhausen) as a hypothetical variant-set view only; the default_visible-true baseline now splits Schaffhausen out per the historical-founding mandate.

pole.note: Same polycentric structure as the reduced record, with Schaffhausen included as an additional secondary pole in this view.

parliament.name: Kantonsraete of all 13 member cantons
parliament.note: Hypothetical combined variant view; not an actual administrative unit.

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Lucerne, St. Gallen, plus Schaffhausen in this combined view
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: finance, textiles, Alpine tourism, precision manufacturing, Rhine Falls tourism
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: hypothetical combined framing for toggle purposes only

autarky.rationale: Identical profile to the reduced ch-central-eastern record; Schaffhausen's small population does not materially shift the composite.

rationales.water: Same Alpine-headwater abundance as the reduced record, plus the Rhine at Schaffhausen.
rationales.food: Same mid-range profile as the reduced record.
rationales.energy: Same strong hydropower-driven score, plus the small Rhine Falls generation asset.

regions.name: Schaffhausen
regions.identity_basis: Switzerland's northernmost canton, a Rhine-enclave founding-era canton (joined the Confederacy in 1501) with its own distinct civic history separate from the later Ostschweiz statistical grouping it is usually lumped into; split out as its own cultural unit in v0.1.2 per the plan's historical-founding rationale.
regions.population_note: Swiss Federal Statistical Office (BFS) 2023 estimate, Canton of Schaffhausen; split from the former ch-central-eastern total (2,028,000 for 13 cantons) using the canton's own population.
regions.nuts1_disagreement: Matches SR2024 CH052 exactly. Previously folded into ch-central-eastern's broad Zentral-/Ostschweiz combination in v0.1.0; split out in draft_v0.1.2 per the explicit mandate honoring Schaffhausen's distinct 1501 founding-era canton history (it is a Rhine-enclave, near-exclave canton, almost entirely surrounded by Germany on three sides) rather than treating it as an undifferentiated part of Ostschweiz. See the schaffhausen variant set for the alternative 'within Ostschweiz' framing.

pole.note: Schaffhausen town is the sole urban center of this small canton.

parliament.name: Kantonsrat Schaffhausen
parliament.note: Single-canton unit; own cantonal parliament.

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Schaffhausen town (~37,000) -- historic Rhine-crossing city, seat of the cantonal government
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: precision manufacturing, Rhine Falls tourism (Europe's largest plain waterfall), cross-border trade, viticulture
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: distinct Schaffhausen cantonal identity within the Confederation, historically separate from the Zentral-/Ostschweiz grouping it is statistically bundled with; no separatism

autarky.rationale: The Rhine gives abundant water and a hydropower asset at the Rhine Falls; a small, near-exclave canton has limited farmland and a thin specialist-healthcare base relative to Zuerich/Basel.

rationales.water: The Rhine (and the Rhine Falls hydropower plant) gives abundant per-capita supply.
rationales.food: Small canton with limited farmland beyond viticulture; not surplus-scale.
rationales.energy: The Rhine Falls hydropower station gives a small but genuine domestic generation asset.

regions.name: Ticino
regions.identity_basis: Switzerland's sole Italian-speaking canton; a Lombard-Alpine cultural identity oriented toward Milan, distinct from both German- and French-speaking Switzerland.
regions.population_note: Swiss Federal Statistical Office (BFS) 2023 estimate, Canton of Ticino

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Lugano -- Switzerland's third-largest financial center
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: private banking, tourism, Gotthard-corridor logistics
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: distinct Italian-speaking Ticinese identity within the Confederation; no separatism

autarky.rationale: Alpine water is abundant; the Gotthard Base Tunnel gives Ticino disproportionate transportation self-sufficiency for its size; private banking and tourism give a diversified but energy-import-dependent profile.

rationales.water: Alpine and lake (Lugano/Maggiore) water is abundant.
rationales.food: Limited valley-floor arable land; wine and chestnut culture are real but not surplus-scale.
rationales.energy: Alpine hydropower and the Gotthard-corridor grid infrastructure keep energy mid-to-strong.

pole.note: Lugano is Switzerland's third-largest financial center and dominant Ticinese hub.

parliament.name: Gran Consiglio della Repubblica e Cantone Ticino
parliament.note: Single-canton unit; own cantonal parliament.

regions.name: Liechtenstein
regions.identity_basis: Sovereign Principality; a German-speaking Alemannic micro-state closely tied economically to Switzerland (currency union, customs union) yet politically fully independent.
regions.population_note: Liechtenstein Office of Statistics (Amt fuer Statistik) 2023 estimate, national population

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Vaduz -- capital, seat of government and princely residence
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: financial services, precision manufacturing, dental/medical technology
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: sovereign Liechtenstein national identity; not seeking independence -- it already has it -- the single-unit exception here reflects micro-state scale, not a subordinate identity

autarky.rationale: A small, wealthy, import-dependent micro-state for food and bulk goods; the Swiss currency/customs union and shared electricity grid support a comfortable but import-linked energy and transportation profile; precision manufacturing gives strong healthcare-adjacent (dental/medical device) capacity.

rationales.water: Rhine-valley and Alpine catchments are abundant relative to the tiny population.
rationales.food: A small, wealthy micro-state with negligible domestic agriculture; structurally import-dependent.
rationales.energy: Shares the Swiss grid/customs union; no significant domestic generation asset.

sources: Liechtenstein Office of Statistics (Amt fuer Statistik)

pole.note: Vaduz is the seat of government and princely residence.

parliament.name: Landtag des Fuerstentums Liechtenstein
parliament.note: Sovereign national parliament.

regions.name: Paris & Île-de-France
regions.identity_basis: The historic royal domaine/couronne around Paris; not a dialect region but a capital-region identity built on centralized administrative, cultural and economic primacy within the French state.
regions.population_note: Eurostat/INSEE 2023 estimate, sum FR101-FR108 (all 8 départements of Île-de-France)

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Paris — metro >12M, the EU's largest urban agglomeration outside London/Moscow
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: finance (La Défense), luxury/fashion (LVMH, Kering HQs), aerospace/defense, publishing, tourism
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: capital-region identity fully integrated into the French state; no separatism, though a distinct 'Parisien vs. province' cultural friction is widely noted

autarky.rationale: Dense capital region imports most food and energy from the wider Bassin Parisien and national grid; land scarcity keeps housing supply and food self-sufficiency low despite outer Grande Couronne wheat farming. World-class transport (Roissy, Orly, TGV hub) and hospital/university-medicine capacity are the region's clear strengths.

rationales.water: Seine-basin abstraction plus the large upstream Grands Lacs de Seine reservoirs cover supply, but 12M consumers leave little buffer in drought years — mid score.
rationales.food: Grande Couronne grain farming is real but feeds only a fraction of 12M residents; the region depends structurally on Bassin Parisien and national food logistics.
rationales.energy: No significant generation inside the région; electricity and gas are imported wholesale from the national grid (the supplying nuclear plants sit outside Île-de-France).

pole.note: Textbook monopole: Paris dominates the unit and the whole French state (capital primacy).

reach.note: National capital primacy: administrative, financial, media and transport reach extends over the entire French territory, well beyond Île-de-France.

parliament.name: Conseil régional d'Île-de-France
parliament.note: Administrative region council, not a legislative parliament (France is a unitary state).

regions.name: Hauts-de-France (Lille/Nord)
regions.identity_basis: Merges the former Nord-Pas-de-Calais (Picard/Ch'ti dialect area, coal-mining and textile heritage) with Picardie; Nord-Pas-de-Calais carries the stronger, more distinct regional identity of the two.
regions.population_note: Eurostat/INSEE 2023 estimate, sum FRE1+FRE2 (Nord-Pas-de-Calais + Picardie)

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Lille — metro ~1.2M, cross-border hub with Belgium (Eurostar/Eurotunnel node)
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: automotive (Toyota, Renault), rail (Bombardier/Alstom), agri-food, logistics via Dunkirk/Calais ports
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: strong Ch'ti/Picard cultural identity within France; no separatism

regions.nuts1_disagreement: NUTS-1 FRE (Hauts-de-France, 2016 merger of Nord-Pas-de-Calais + Picardie) is kept whole here rather than split: Picardie's own urban hub (Amiens, metro ~180,000) is real but does not clear a comparable bar to Lille, and the zone's region-count budget favors treating it as Lille's hinterland.

autarky.rationale: Hosts Gravelines, Western Europe's largest nuclear power station, giving very high energy self-sufficiency, alongside some of France's most productive grain and sugar-beet farmland. Historic Lille-Roubaix-Tourcoing textile heritage supports a modest residual clothing/design base; Channel ports (Calais, Dunkirk) anchor transportation.

rationales.water: Chalk-aquifer groundwater of the Artois-Picardie basin covers most demand; industrial-legacy pollution pressures quality, not quantity.
rationales.food: Among France's most productive arable land: wheat, sugar beet and potatoes at surplus scale relative to the regional population.
rationales.energy: Gravelines (6 reactors, Western Europe's largest nuclear plant) plus the Dunkirk LNG terminal make the region a structural net electricity exporter.

pole.note: Lille dominates; Amiens is a real but clearly subordinate Picard secondary center.

reach.target: Belgian Flanders and Wallonia (Kortrijk, Tournai, Mouscron)
reach.note: Lille's functional urban area crosses the border: the Eurométropole Lille-Kortrijk-Tournai (first European Grouping of Territorial Cooperation, 2008) institutionalizes ~2.1M inhabitants of cross-border catchment.

parliament.name: Conseil régional des Hauts-de-France
parliament.note: Administrative region council, not a legislative parliament.

regions.name: Normandy
regions.identity_basis: Historic Duchy of Normandy; residual Norman dialect (langue d'oïl branch) and a strong maritime/D-Day-heritage regional identity, reunified administratively in 2016 after the 1956 Haute/Basse split.
regions.population_note: Eurostat/INSEE 2023 estimate, sum FRD1+FRD2 (Basse- + Haute-Normandie, reunified NUTS-1 FRD)

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Rouen — metro ~660,000; Le Havre is France's second-largest container port
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: dairy/cider agri-food, automotive supply, petrochemicals, two nuclear plants
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: Norman regional identity and D-Day/maritime heritage within France; no separatism

sources: Regional Council of Normandy heritage/identity documentation

autarky.rationale: Dense dairy, cider and livestock farming (Camembert, Calvados) plus nuclear plants (Flamanville, Paluel, Penly) give Normandy strong food and energy scores; Le Havre and Cherbourg add real port-based transport capacity. Clothing manufacture is negligible, as in most of deindustrialized northern France.

rationales.water: Atlantic-facing rainfall and the Seine/Orne river systems provide reliable supply; no structural scarcity.
rationales.food: One of Europe's densest dairy/livestock landscapes (Camembert, Pont-l'Évêque, cider/Calvados) plus grain in the Caen plain — clear surplus producer.
rationales.energy: Three coastal nuclear sites (Flamanville incl. the EPR, Paluel, Penly) plus Le Havre refining make the region a heavy net energy exporter.

pole.note: Historic Haute/Basse-Normandie dipole survives reunification: Rouen holds the prefecture, Caen hosts the conseil régional seat.

parliament.name: Conseil régional de Normandie
parliament.note: Administrative region council, not a legislative parliament.

regions.name: Brittany
regions.identity_basis: Breton language (Brythonic Celtic, distinct from the surrounding langue d'oïl area) and historic Duchy of Brittany; one of France's most distinct regional identities, with an active (non-separatist) cultural-autonomy movement.
regions.population_note: Eurostat/INSEE 2023 estimate, sum FRH01-FRH04

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Rennes — metro ~750,000, major tech/telecom cluster
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: agri-food (France's top livestock region), fishing fleet, naval defense, digital services
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: strong Breton linguistic/cultural identity within France; regionalist movement (Bonnets Rouges, Breton-language schools) is cultural-autonomist, not separatist

regions.nuts1_disagreement: NUTS-1 FRH matches historic Brittany minus the Loire-Atlantique/Nantes département, which was administratively detached in 1941 and sits in Pays de la Loire (FRG) in this dataset — a long-standing 'Réunification de la Bretagne' grievance noted but not redrawn here, consistent with current NUTS boundaries.
sources: RTE (French grid operator) Brittany energy-security reports

autarky.rationale: France's top agri-food peninsula (pork, poultry, dairy) gives Brittany strong food self-sufficiency, but it hosts no nuclear plant and is structurally electricity-import-dependent via the mainland grid — a long-standing regional energy-security concern flagged by RTE. Coastal water abundance and Brest/Saint-Malo ports are solid; clothing production is minimal.

rationales.water: High Atlantic rainfall and a dense small-river network; nitrate pollution from intensive livestock constrains quality, not quantity.
rationales.food: France's leading livestock region (roughly half of national pork output, plus poultry, dairy, vegetables) — large structural surplus.
rationales.energy: No nuclear or major thermal plant on the peninsula; RTE has repeatedly flagged Brittany as an electricity-security 'peninsula' importing most of its power.

pole.note: Rennes organizes eastern Brittany and the region administratively; Brest is a strong western maritime counterweight but clearly second.

parliament.name: Conseil régional de Bretagne
parliament.note: Administrative region council, not a legislative parliament (despite the cultural-autonomy movement seeking more).

regions.name: Pays de la Loire (Loire/Nantes)
regions.identity_basis: Nantes-Saint-Nazaire industrial/Atlantic identity merged here with the Val de Loire chateaux corridor (Orléans-Tours); both share the Loire river as a geographic and cultural spine.
regions.population_note: Eurostat/INSEE 2023 estimate, sum FRG01-05 (Pays de la Loire) + FRB01-06 (Centre-Val de Loire)

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Nantes — metro ~970,000, one of France's fastest-growing cities
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: aerospace (Airbus Nantes/Saint-Nazaire), shipbuilding, cosmetics/pharma (Cosmetic Valley), agri-food
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: regional pride tied to Loire-Atlantique/Nantes and Val de Loire heritage within France; no separatism

regions.nuts1_disagreement: Centre-Val de Loire (NUTS-1 FRB) is a genuine NUTS-1 unit but lacks a sufficiently distinct sub-national identity — it sits in the historic Francien-dialect core with no strong separate provincial boundary — relative to the zone's other listed anchors. It is folded into Pays de la Loire via the shared Loire-valley/chateaux corridor (Orléans-Tours-Angers-Nantes). Re-checked in v0.1.2 against the Auvergne/Burgundy/Champagne split logic: kept merged, because neither Orléans nor Tours presents an organizing-pole case comparable to Clermont-Ferrand or Reims — the Loire corridor genuinely chains these cities into one axis.
sources: INSEE (Pays de la Loire and Centre-Val de Loire regional statistics)
RTE nuclear generation data by département

autarky.rationale: Combines Pays de la Loire's Nantes-Saint-Nazaire industrial/agri base with Centre-Val de Loire's cluster of Loire nuclear plants (Chinon, Saint-Laurent, Dampierre, Belleville), pushing the merged region's energy self-sufficiency to among the highest in the zone; grain and market-garden farming along the Loire corridor supports solid food scores.

rationales.water: The Loire and its tributaries plus Atlantic-facing rainfall cover demand; summer low-flow episodes on the Loire occasionally constrain nuclear cooling and irrigation.
rationales.food: Beauce grain plains ('granary of France', Centre-Val de Loire component) plus Loire-Atlantique livestock and market gardening — solid surplus.
rationales.energy: Four Loire-valley nuclear plants (Chinon, Saint-Laurent, Dampierre, Belleville) inside the unit's codes make it a major net electricity exporter.

pole.note: Nantes organizes the Atlantic end; Tours and Orléans are genuine mid-Loire poles of the merged Centre-Val de Loire component — the unit reads as a Loire-corridor chain rather than one catchment.

parliament.name: Conseil régional des Pays de la Loire; Conseil régional du Centre-Val de Loire
parliament.note: Two administrative region councils (the unit spans two administrative régions); neither is a legislative parliament.

regions.name: Aquitaine (incl. Poitou-Charentes, Limousin)
regions.identity_basis: Gascon/Occitan-language southwest French identity centered on Bordeaux wine culture, extended to the historic Poitou and Limousin provinces via the medieval Duchy of Aquitaine. Auvergne, formerly folded in here, is split out as its own unit in v0.1.2 (Clermont-Ferrand ≠ Bordeaux).
regions.population_note: Eurostat/INSEE 2023 estimate, sum FRI11-15 + FRI21-23 + FRI31-34 (Nouvelle-Aquitaine, NUTS-1 FRI); Auvergne (FRK11-14) removed in the v0.1.2 split

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Bordeaux — metro ~1M, dominant hub of the French southwest
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: wine/agri-food (Bordeaux, Cognac), aerospace/defense (Dassault), nuclear energy, insurance (Niort)
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: Gascon/Occitan regional identity within France; no separatism

regions.nuts1_disagreement: NUTS-1 FRI (Nouvelle-Aquitaine) is kept whole rather than split into its three historic components (Aquitaine, Poitou-Charentes, Limousin), since neither Poitiers/La Rochelle nor Limoges clears the urban-hub bar independently at the zone's target granularity. The v0.1.0 addition of Auvergne (FRK1) to this unit is REVERSED in v0.1.2 per user mandate — see fr-auvergne.

conflict_flags.description: The French Basque Country (Iparralde/Pays Basque) forms a cultural micro-layer within Pyrénées-Atlantiques (FRI15), alongside the distinct, non-Basque Béarnais territory in the same département. A unified cross-border Basque region (Euskadi + Navarre + Iparralde) is modeled in zone3 ('basque-unified', shown via the zone3 basque variant set), reusing this NUTS-3 code without altering Aquitaine's own boundaries here.

autarky.rationale: Bordeaux wine/aerospace anchors a diversified base; the Blayais nuclear plant (Gironde) and abundant Pyrenean/Atlantic water keep energy and water scores solid, while Nouvelle-Aquitaine's status as France's largest farming region (grain, wine, livestock, Cognac) supports strong food self-sufficiency.

rationales.water: Garonne/Dordogne/Charente basins plus Pyrenean runoff and high Atlantic rainfall; increasing summer irrigation tension in the Charentes is noted but not yet structural scarcity.
rationales.food: France's largest farming region by output value: grain, wine (Bordeaux, Cognac), maize, poultry (Landes), oysters (Marennes) — strong surplus.
rationales.energy: Blayais nuclear plant (4 reactors, Gironde estuary) covers regional demand with margin; growing solar capacity in the Landes supplements it.

pole.note: Bordeaux dominates the southwest; Limoges and Poitiers are subordinate provincial centers.

parliament.name: Conseil régional de Nouvelle-Aquitaine
parliament.note: Administrative region council, not a legislative parliament.

regions.name: Auvergne (Clermont-Ferrand)
regions.identity_basis: Historic province of Auvergne in the volcanic heart of the Massif Central; Auvergnat Occitan dialect (north-Occitan branch) and a strong upland pastoral identity (Cantal/Saint-Nectaire cheese country), organized around Clermont-Ferrand and its Michelin industrial anchor. Split out of Aquitaine in v0.1.2 per user mandate: Clermont-Ferrand's Einzugsgebiet (catchment) never pointed to Bordeaux.
key_industries: agri-food (AOP cheeses: Cantal, Saint-Nectaire, Bleu d'Auvergne)
regions.population_note: Eurostat/INSEE 2023 estimate, sum FRK11-14 (Allier, Cantal, Haute-Loire, Puy-de-Dôme)

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Clermont-Ferrand — metro ~500,000, global HQ of Michelin and clear organizing center of the Massif Central; modest for a standalone unit but unambiguous as the region's hub
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: Michelin tyre/rubber R&D and manufacturing, AOP cheese/livestock agri-food, Volvic mineral water, Issoire aerospace metallurgy, Vichy spa economy
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: Auvergnat (north-Occitan) upland identity within France; no separatism

regions.nuts1_disagreement: Auvergne is NUTS-2 FRK1 within NUTS-1 FRK (Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes, 2016 merger). It is authored standalone here: the v0.1.0 grouping with Aquitaine (Massif Central/Limousin contiguity) was rejected by user feedback ('Clermont-Ferrand ≠ Bordeaux'), and the merger with Rhône-Alpes is offered only as a variant-set view (fused ARA bloc, fr-auvergne-rhone-alpes), not as the default cultural unit.

autarky.rationale: Massif Central headwaters (Loire, Allier, Dordogne all rise here) and famous aquifers (Volvic) give top water scores; upland livestock/cheese farming plus Limagne-plain grain support solid food self-sufficiency for only 1.37M people. Landlocked mid-mountain terrain with no TGV line keeps transportation the weak dimension; energy relies on hydro and imports (no nuclear plant).

rationales.water: The Massif Central is France's water tower: Loire, Allier and Dordogne headwaters plus volcanic aquifers (Volvic) — abundant supply for a small population.
rationales.food: Extensive upland livestock and five AOP cheeses plus Limagne-plain cereals comfortably exceed the needs of 1.37M inhabitants.
rationales.energy: No nuclear or major thermal plant; modest hydro and wind mean structural electricity imports, partly offset by low regional demand.

pole.note: Clermont-Ferrand is the unrivalled hub; Vichy/Montluçon/Aurillac are small subordinate towns.

parliament.name: Conseil régional d'Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes (shared, seat Lyon)
parliament.note: Administrative region council, not a legislative parliament; since 2016 Auvergne shares it with Rhône-Alpes — the historic Conseil régional d'Auvergne (Clermont-Ferrand) was merged away, which is itself part of the identity grievance behind this split.

regions.name: Midi-Pyrénées (Toulouse/Occitanie-west)
regions.identity_basis: Western Occitanie, Occitan-language (Languedocien/Gascon-transition) area anchored on Toulouse ('la Ville Rose'); deliberately treated as distinct from the eastern, Montpellier-anchored Languedoc-Roussillon component of the merged NUTS-1 Occitanie region.
regions.population_note: Eurostat/INSEE 2023 estimate, sum FRJ21-28 (former Midi-Pyrénées, now NUTS-2 FRJ2 within Occitanie)

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Toulouse — metro ~1.5M, Europe's aerospace-industry capital
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: civil aerospace (Airbus), space (CNES/Thales Alenia), agri-food, nuclear energy
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: Occitan-language regional identity within France; no separatism

regions.nuts1_disagreement: NUTS-1 FRJ (Occitanie, 2016 merger of Midi-Pyrénées + Languedoc-Roussillon) is split here into its two historic components: the zone brief's own 'Toulouse/Occitanie-west' label signals a deliberate west/east distinction, and Montpellier independently clears the urban-hub and industry bar with a genuinely distinct Mediterranean identity layer.

autarky.rationale: Aerospace (Airbus Toulouse) is a manufacturing/export strength rather than a survival good, so autarky rests more on diversified agriculture (Gers foie gras/wine, Aveyron cattle) and the Golfech nuclear plant (Tarn-et-Garonne); Pyrenean water reserves are ample, but the region lacks a major seaport, holding transportation to a middling score.

rationales.water: Garonne headwaters and Pyrenean snowpack feed reliable supply plus substantial hydro reservoirs; summer irrigation draw on the Garonne is a managed tension.
rationales.food: Diversified surplus agriculture: Gers poultry/foie gras, Aveyron cattle, Lauragais grain, Fronton/Gaillac wine.
rationales.energy: Golfech nuclear plant plus dense Pyrenean hydropower give near self-sufficiency in electricity.

pole.note: Toulouse utterly dominates — no secondary city in the unit exceeds ~80,000.

parliament.name: Conseil régional d'Occitanie (shared, seat Toulouse)
parliament.note: Administrative region council, not a legislative parliament; shared with the Languedoc-Roussillon unit since the 2016 merger, seated in Toulouse.

regions.name: Languedoc-Roussillon (Montpellier)
regions.identity_basis: Eastern, Mediterranean-facing Occitanie, Languedocien-Occitan speaking, with a distinct Catalan-language minority layer in Roussillon (Perpignan/Pyrénées-Orientales) bordering Catalonia.
key_industries: viticulture (Languedoc wine, world's largest single wine-growing area)
regions.population_note: Eurostat/INSEE 2023 estimate, sum FRJ11-15 (former Languedoc-Roussillon, now NUTS-2 FRJ1 within Occitanie)

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Montpellier — metro ~650,000, France's fastest-growing major city over the past two decades
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: viticulture, digital/health-tech cluster, tourism, solar energy
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: Occitan/Languedocien identity plus a distinct Catalan-speaking Roussillon minority; no separatism

regions.nuts1_disagreement: See fr-midi-pyrenees: this region is the eastern half of the merged NUTS-1 Occitanie, split out as its own node because it independently clears the inclusion test rather than being absorbed as Toulouse's hinterland.
sources: Institut Français de Catalogne Nord (Roussillon Catalan minority documentation)

autarky.rationale: A major wine region with limited staple-food output and no nuclear generation, Languedoc-Roussillon scores only moderately on food and low on energy; Mediterranean drought pressure and irrigation-dependent viticulture strain water, while Montpellier's rapid urban growth adds further land/shelter pressure rather than easing it.

rationales.water: Mediterranean drought regime with recurring summer restrictions; the Rhône-to-Montpellier Aqua Domitia canal partially de-risks supply but dependence on transfers caps the score.
rationales.food: Vast wine output but thin staple production (grain, dairy) on the dry coastal plain — wine does not feed a region.
rationales.energy: No nuclear or major thermal plant in the unit; growing solar and wind but still a structural electricity importer from the Rhône valley.

pole.note: Montpellier leads; Nîmes and Perpignan are sizeable but clearly within its regional orbit (Perpignan retains a distinct Catalan orientation).

parliament.name: Conseil régional d'Occitanie (shared, seat Toulouse)
parliament.note: Administrative region council, not a legislative parliament; shared with Midi-Pyrénées, seated in Toulouse (assembly sessions in Montpellier).

regions.name: Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur
regions.identity_basis: Provençal identity (historic County of Provence, Provençal-Occitan dialect) spanning the Mediterranean coast from Marseille to Nice/Côte d'Azur.
regions.population_note: Eurostat/INSEE 2023 estimate, sum FRL01-06

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Marseille — metro ~1.9M, France's largest port and second-largest city
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: port/logistics, petrochemicals, tourism (Côte d'Azur), energy research (ITER), perfume industry
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: Provençal regional identity within France; no separatism

sources: Grand Port Maritime de Marseille annual report

autarky.rationale: Marseille's port and airport, plus the Cadarache/ITER research-energy complex, give reasonable transport and energy footing, but dense Riviera urbanization and recurring Mediterranean drought constrain food, water and shelter; Marseille's major hospital and university-medicine base lifts healthcare capacity to the zone's top tier.

rationales.water: Durance/Verdon transfers (Canal de Provence) engineered around a structurally dry Mediterranean climate; supply holds but depends on Alpine snowpack in decline.
rationales.food: Fruit/vegetable and wine specialization on scarce coastal land; staples are imported — the region cannot feed 5M from its own territory.
rationales.energy: Durance hydro chain and Fos petrochemical/LNG infrastructure give partial coverage; no nuclear generation, so net imports remain.

pole.note: Marseille organizes Provence proper; Nice/Côte d'Azur (historic County of Nice, Italian until 1860) is a genuinely separate eastern pole rather than a suburb.

parliament.name: Conseil régional de Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur
parliament.note: Administrative region council, not a legislative parliament.

regions.name: Rhône-Alpes (Lyon)
regions.identity_basis: Lyon's historic identity as France's 'second city' and the Rhône-Alpine industrial/Alpine base (Franco-Provençal/Arpitan substrate area). Bourgogne-Franche-Comté, folded in here in v0.1.0, is split out as its own unit in v0.1.2 — Valence (Rhône valley) and Auxerre (Yonne) never belonged to one catchment.
regions.population_note: Eurostat/INSEE 2023 estimate, sum FRK21-28 (Rhône-Alpes); Bourgogne-Franche-Comté (FRC) removed in the v0.1.2 split

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Lyon — metro ~2.3M, France's second-largest urban area
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: chemicals/pharma, nuclear energy, microelectronics (Grenoble/STMicroelectronics), machinery, Beaujolais/Côtes du Rhône wine
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: Lyonnais and Franco-Provençal (Arpitan) substrate identity within France; no separatism

regions.nuts1_disagreement: Per the v0.1.0 mandate, Rhône-Alpes (NUTS-2 FRK2) is kept independent of Auvergne (now its own unit fr-auvergne; the fused ARA bloc exists only as a variant-set view). The v0.1.0 folding-in of Bourgogne-Franche-Comté (FRC) is REVERSED in v0.1.2 per user feedback ('Valence ≠ Auxerre') — see fr-burgundy-franche-comte.

autarky.rationale: Alpine water reserves, three nuclear plants (Bugey, Saint-Alban, Cruas) plus Rhône hydro, and Lyon's rail/air/river hub status combine for the zone's strongest overall profile; Rhône valley orchards, Bresse poultry and Beaujolais wine keep food solid, and Lyon's silk/textile heritage leaves a residual clothing-industry edge.

rationales.water: Alpine snowpack, Lake Geneva/Annecy reserves and the Rhône itself — among the most water-rich units in the dataset.
rationales.food: Rhône-valley fruit/vegetables, Bresse poultry (AOP), alpine dairy and Beaujolais vineyards give a diversified near-surplus for 6.8M people.
rationales.energy: Three nuclear plants (Bugey, Saint-Alban, Cruas) plus the Rhône hydro cascade make this one of Europe's largest net electricity-exporting regions.

pole.note: Lyon dominates; Grenoble and Saint-Étienne are large but functionally within Lyon's regional system.

parliament.name: Conseil régional d'Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes (seat Lyon)
parliament.note: Administrative region council, not a legislative parliament; shared with the Auvergne unit since the 2016 merger.

regions.name: Burgundy–Franche-Comté (Dijon/Besançon)
regions.identity_basis: Historic Duchy of Burgundy (Dijon, Côte d'Or wine culture, Bourguignon oïl dialect) joined with the Franche-Comté ('free county' of Burgundy — Besançon, Jura watchmaking/microtechnique, Comtois identity shaped by centuries outside the French crown until 1678). Split out of the Lyon unit in v0.1.2: the Saône corridor links them commercially, but Auxerre and the Yonne drain toward the Paris basin and neither Dijon nor Besançon sits in Lyon's Einzugsgebiet — fixing the user-flagged 'Valence ≠ Auxerre' over-stretch.
regions.population_note: Eurostat/INSEE 2023 estimate, sum FRC11-14 (Bourgogne) + FRC21-24 (Franche-Comté)

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Dijon — metro ~400,000, historic Burgundian capital and the unit's administrative center; Besançon (~280,000) is a genuine second pole with its own Comtois identity
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: world-brand viticulture (Burgundy), automotive (Sochaux, PSA's historic plant), precision microtechnique/watchmaking, Comté/Charolais agri-food, rail equipment (Alstom)
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: Bourguignon and Comtois identities within France; no separatism — identity strength is regional-historical (duchy/county heritage) rather than linguistic

regions.nuts1_disagreement: NUTS-1 FRC (Bourgogne-Franche-Comté) is authored as one standalone unit rather than split into Burgundy and Franche-Comté: the two halves were merged administratively in 2016, share the Saône axis, and neither Dijon nor Besançon dominates the other — modeled as a dipole instead. Its v0.1.0 absorption into fr-rhone-alpes is REVERSED per user feedback.
sources: Comité interprofessionnel du Comté (AOP filière statistics)

autarky.rationale: Charolais beef, Comté/Morbier dairy filières, Burgundy grain and world-price viticulture give comfortable food self-sufficiency for 2.8M people, and low density leaves shelter headroom; the Paris-Lyon rail/motorway spine and Saône waterway support transport. The clear weakness is energy: no nuclear or major thermal plant operates in the unit, leaving it dependent on imports from neighboring regions.

rationales.water: Saône/Doubs river systems, Jura karst springs and Morvan reservoirs provide reliable supply with low demand pressure.
rationales.food: Charolais beef, AOP Comté dairy, Burgundy/Chablis wine and Yonne cereals — a clear net food exporter.
rationales.energy: No power plant of scale in either half; electricity is imported from Rhône-valley nuclear and eastern hydro — the unit's weakest dimension.

pole.note: Dijon (Burgundy, administrative seat) and Besançon (Franche-Comté, university/microtechnique) form a genuine dipole reflecting the 2016 merger of two historic territories.

parliament.name: Conseil régional de Bourgogne-Franche-Comté (seat Dijon/Besançon)
parliament.note: Administrative region council, not a legislative parliament; council seat split between Dijon (assembly) and Besançon (offices) — institutionalizing the dipole.

regions.name: Alsace
regions.identity_basis: Alsatian (Elsässisch, Alemannic-German dialect) linguistic identity; historic back-and-forth between France and Germany (1871-1918, 1940-1945) gives Alsace one of France's most distinct regional identities, standalone per the zone brief mandate despite being folded into Grand Est administratively since 2016.
regions.population_note: Eurostat/INSEE 2023 estimate, sum FRF11+FRF12 (Bas-Rhin + Haut-Rhin)

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Strasbourg — metro ~800,000, seat of the European Parliament and Council of Europe
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: automotive, wine, chemicals, EU-institution administration/services
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: Alemannic Alsatian identity within France; no separatism despite the historically contested Franco-German border status

regions.nuts1_disagreement: NUTS-1 FRF (Grand Est, 2016 merger of Alsace + Champagne-Ardenne + Lorraine) is split here per the zone brief's explicit mandate to keep Alsace standalone. In v0.1.2 the other two Grand-Est fragments are ALSO separated from each other (fr-lorraine, fr-champagne) — the full 2016 merger is now fully unwound in this dataset.
sources: INSEE (Grand Est regional statistics, Alsace sub-detail)

autarky.rationale: The Fessenheim nuclear plant's 2020 closure moved Alsace from a former energy surplus to grid dependence, though the Rhine hydro cascade partly compensates; fertile Rhine-plain agriculture (wine, hops, market gardens) and Strasbourg's EU-institution transport links remain solid strengths.

rationales.water: The Rhine and one of Europe's largest groundwater bodies (Upper Rhine aquifer) underlie the plain — abundant, with some legacy potash-salination monitoring.
rationales.food: Fertile Rhine-plain agriculture: wine, hops, cabbage/market gardens plus cereals — comfortably feeds the region with surplus specialty exports.
rationales.energy: Post-Fessenheim (closed 2020) the region imports most electricity; Rhine run-of-river hydro shared with Germany covers only part of demand.

pole.note: Strasbourg dominates; Mulhouse anchors the industrial south but within Strasbourg's regional orbit.

parliament.name: Collectivité européenne d'Alsace (assembly); Conseil régional du Grand Est
parliament.note: The Collectivité européenne d'Alsace (since 2021) restored an Alsace-wide elected assembly with departmental + some devolved powers — still an administrative council, not a legislative parliament; regional-council competences sit with Grand Est (Strasbourg seat).

regions.name: Lorraine
regions.identity_basis: Historic Duchy of Lorraine (Francique Lorrain/Lorrain dialect in the Moselle east, langue d'oïl elsewhere), organized around the Nancy-Metz twin cities and the post-steel Moselle industrial valley. Champagne-Ardenne, folded in here in v0.1.0 as the 'other non-Alsace Grand-Est fragment', is split out as fr-champagne in v0.1.2 (see zone notes for the verdict).
regions.population_note: Eurostat/INSEE 2023 estimate, sum FRF31-34 (Meurthe-et-Moselle, Meuse, Moselle, Vosges); Champagne-Ardenne (FRF21-24) removed in the v0.1.2 split

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Nancy-Metz — combined metro ~1.1M, a classic twin-city (dipole) system 50 km apart
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: nuclear energy (Cattenom), post-steel advanced materials, cross-border services economy (100k+ daily commuters to Luxembourg), Vosges timber, agri-food
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: Lorrain regional identity within France (with a Germanic Francique fringe along the Moselle border); no separatism

regions.nuts1_disagreement: Lorraine is NUTS-2 FRF3 within NUTS-1 FRF (Grand Est).
