regions.population_note: Eurostat 2023 estimate (ISTAT), Veneto NUTS-2 ITH3

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Venice — globally iconic historic-maritime capital; Verona/Padua as secondary economic hubs
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: tourism, gold/jewelry manufacturing (Vicenza), furniture (Treviso), Prosecco viticulture, leather/footwear
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: strong Venetian regional identity with an active but non-secessionist autonomy movement

autarky.rationale: Po Valley plain and Prosecco hills give solid food self-sufficiency; Venice's lagoon geography creates unique but manageable water/shelter vulnerabilities (acqua alta flooding, MOSE barrier).

rationales.water: Po Valley plain and Dolomite headwaters give solid supply, moderated by Venice's lagoon-specific vulnerabilities.
rationales.food: Po Valley agriculture and Prosecco-hill viticulture give strong self-sufficiency.
rationales.energy: Limited domestic generation; industrial SME base (Vicenza, Treviso) is a net energy importer.

pole.note: Veneto's 'città diffusa' settlement pattern: Verona/Padua/Vicenza are economically comparable to Venice, which retains symbolic/political centrality.

parliament.name: Consiglio regionale del Veneto
parliament.note: Italian region with its own Consiglio regionale (regional council/parliament).

regions.name: Friuli-Venezia Giulia
regions.identity_basis: Special-statute autonomous region with a trilingual heritage (Friulian, Italian, Slovene) and Trieste's distinct Habsburg-port history at the head of the Adriatic; mandated standalone per global constraints.
regions.population_note: Eurostat 2023 estimate (ISTAT), Friuli-Venezia Giulia NUTS-2 ITH4

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Trieste — former Habsburg imperial port, insurance/finance hub with a distinctive Central European character
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: port logistics, insurance (Generali), furniture manufacturing (Udine), shipbuilding/marine tech
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: special-statute autonomy reflecting Friulian and Slovene minority presence, no separatism

autarky.rationale: Trieste's port and Central European trade links give strong transportation self-sufficiency; Friulian plain agriculture supports moderate food self-sufficiency for a small special-statute region.

rationales.water: Friulian plain rivers and Alpine headwaters give ample supply for a small population.
rationales.food: Friulian-plain agriculture supports moderate self-sufficiency for a small special-statute region.
rationales.energy: Trieste's port/trade role is not matched by domestic generation; net importer.

pole.note: Trieste: port/political capital; Udine: inland historic Friulian cultural capital.

parliament.name: Consiglio regionale del Friuli Venezia Giulia
parliament.note: Italian region with its own Consiglio regionale (regional council/parliament). Special-statute region (regione a statuto speciale) with enhanced legislative competencies.

regions.nuts1_disagreement: NUTS-1 ITH (Nord-Est) groups South Tyrol with Trentino, Veneto, and Friuli; separated here as its own congruent-variant unit given its distinct German-speaking special-autonomy status.
regions.name: South Tyrol
regions.identity_basis: German-speaking majority special-autonomy province (Austrian until 1918); congruent (Italy-only) variant of the Tyrol toggle group. The unified Tyrol record (joining Austrian Tirol) lives in zone1.json.
regions.population_note: Eurostat 2023 estimate (ASTAT), Provincia Autonoma di Bolzano/Bozen NUTS-2 ITH1

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Bolzano/Bozen — provincial capital, German-Italian bilingual administrative and cultural hub
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: Alpine tourism (Dolomites UNESCO site), apple and wine agriculture, precision manufacturing, hydropower
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: German-speaking majority with full linguistic-cultural autonomy within Italy, an option for Austrian dual citizenship since 2023, historically contested but not currently secessionist

autarky.rationale: Abundant Alpine water and extensive hydropower generation give the highest water and energy scores in the Italian set; mountainous terrain constrains transportation connectivity relative to lowland regions.

rationales.water: Abundant Alpine snowmelt gives the highest water score in the Italian set.
rationales.food: Apple/wine agriculture is strong per capita despite mountainous terrain limiting total arable area.
rationales.energy: Extensive hydropower gives South Tyrol a rare energy-positive position in this dataset.

sources: South Tyrol special-autonomy statute and Austria dual-citizenship provisions (2023)

parliament.name: Landtag Südtirol / Consiglio della Provincia autonoma di Bolzano
parliament.note: Italian region with its own Consiglio regionale (regional council/parliament). Special-statute region (regione a statuto speciale) with enhanced legislative competencies.

regions.name: Trentino
regions.identity_basis: Italian-speaking special-autonomy province, historically and linguistically distinct from German-speaking South Tyrol despite sharing the joint Trentino-Alto Adige/Südtirol regional structure; mandated standalone per zone brief.
regions.population_note: Eurostat 2023 estimate (ISPAT), Provincia Autonoma di Trento NUTS-2 ITH2

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Trento — provincial capital and university/research hub (University of Trento)
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: Alpine tourism, apple/wine agriculture, hydropower, ICT/research (FBK research foundation)
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: distinct Italian-speaking Trentino identity, special autonomy status, no separatism

autarky.rationale: Shares South Tyrol's Alpine water and hydropower abundance; slightly stronger ICT/research diversification via the Trento university-research cluster offsets otherwise similar mountain-region constraints.

rationales.water: Shares South Tyrol's Alpine snowmelt abundance.
rationales.food: Apple/wine agriculture on Alpine valley floors gives solid self-sufficiency.
rationales.energy: Hydropower generation is comparably strong to South Tyrol's.

sources: ISPAT (Istituto di Statistica della Provincia di Trento)

parliament.name: Consiglio della Provincia autonoma di Trento
parliament.note: Italian region with its own Consiglio regionale (regional council/parliament). Special-statute region (regione a statuto speciale) with enhanced legislative competencies.

regions.nuts1_disagreement: NUTS-2 ITH5 (Emilia-Romagna) treats Emilia and Romagna as one administrative region; split here per the mandated Emilia≠Romagna decision. Ferrara (ITH56) is assigned to Emilia rather than Romagna based on Pellegrini's dialect classification placing Ferrarese within the Emiliano group, though Ferrara's historical inclusion in the Papal Legations alongside Ravenna and Forlì is a genuine competing frame — flagged in zone notes for the methodology page.
regions.name: Emilia
regions.identity_basis: Western half of Emilia-Romagna, distinguished from Romagna by the Emiliano dialect group (Pellegrini's Carta dei dialetti d'Italia classifies Ferrara's dialect as Emiliano, not Romagnolo, despite Ferrara's historical Papal-Legation administrative pairing with Ravenna); food-industry and automotive 'Motor Valley' heartland.
key_industries: food processing (Parmigiano-Reggiano, Prosciutto di Parma, balsamic vinegar)
regions.population_note: Eurostat/ISTAT 2023 estimate, sum of NUTS-3 provinces Piacenza+Parma+Reggio Emilia+Modena+Bologna+Ferrara (ITH51-ITH56)

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Bologna — metro ~1M, historic university city (oldest in the Western world) and Emilian cultural-culinary capital
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: world-renowned food-processing PDO/PGI clusters, 'Motor Valley' luxury automotive and motorsport, packaging machinery, biomedical devices
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: distinct Emilian dialect and food-culture identity, no separatism, mandated split from Romagna per project brief

autarky.rationale: Extraordinarily high food self-sufficiency and export strength (Po Valley agriculture plus globally famous PDO food clusters); diversified high-value manufacturing (automotive, packaging machinery, biomedical) gives strong industrial resilience across most dimensions.

rationales.water: Po Valley aquifers and Apennine headwaters give reliable supply for intensive agri-food processing.
rationales.food: World-renowned PDO food clusters (Parmigiano-Reggiano, Prosciutto di Parma) give the dataset's highest food scores.
rationales.energy: Diversified manufacturing (automotive, packaging) is energy-intensive; moderate domestic generation only partly offsets it.

sources: Pellegrini, G.B. (1977) Carta dei dialetti d'Italia — Emiliano/Romagnolo dialect boundary

parliament.name: Assemblea legislativa dell'Emilia-Romagna (shared with Romagna)
parliament.note: Italian region with its own Consiglio regionale (regional council/parliament).

regions.nuts1_disagreement: See Emilia record for the shared NUTS-2 ITH5 disagreement and the Ferrara assignment reasoning.
regions.name: Romagna
regions.identity_basis: Eastern half of Emilia-Romagna, distinguished by the Romagnolo dialect group and a historically separate identity from Emilia (Byzantine Exarchate of Ravenna origin of the name 'Romagna' = 'land of the Romans/Byzantines', vs. Lombard-ruled Emilia); mandated split per project brief.
regions.population_note: Eurostat/ISTAT 2023 estimate, sum of NUTS-3 provinces Ravenna+Forlì-Cesena+Rimini (ITH57-ITH59)

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Ravenna — former Western Roman and Byzantine imperial capital (UNESCO mosaics), Adriatic port; Rimini as mass-tourism hub
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: Adriatic beach tourism (Rimini/Riccione), fruit-and-vegetable food processing, Faenza ceramics (origin of the word 'faience'), Ravenna port and petrochemical complex
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: distinct Romagnolo dialect and post-Byzantine historical identity, culturally proud regionalism ('Romagna, terra di...') but no separatism

autarky.rationale: Adriatic coast tourism and food-processing agriculture give solid but slightly lower composite than Emilia, reflecting smaller scale and heavier tourism-seasonality dependence relative to Emilia's diversified manufacturing base.

rationales.water: Adriatic coastal aquifers are adequate but seasonal tourism spikes demand sharply.
rationales.food: Fruit/vegetable canning and Adriatic fishing give solid, if smaller-scale than Emilia's, self-sufficiency.
rationales.energy: Ravenna's petrochemical/port complex is a significant local energy user with only partial domestic offset.

sources: Pellegrini, G.B. (1977) Carta dei dialetti d'Italia; Romagna historical-identity literature (Exarchate of Ravenna)

pole.note: Ravenna is historic capital (Byzantine Exarchate); Rimini is the larger economic/tourism center — genuinely polycentric.

parliament.name: Assemblea legislativa dell'Emilia-Romagna (shared with Emilia)
parliament.note: Italian region with its own Consiglio regionale (regional council/parliament).

regions.name: Tuscany
regions.identity_basis: Cradle of the Italian Renaissance and of standard Italian itself (Tuscan dialect basis of modern Italian); historic Grand Duchy of Tuscany; globally recognized cultural-agricultural identity (Chianti, Renaissance art cities).
regions.population_note: Eurostat 2023 estimate (ISTAT), Toscana NUTS-2 ITI1

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Florence — metro ~1M, Renaissance capital and UNESCO World Heritage city
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: textiles (Prato's large manufacturing district, including a major Chinese-Italian textile cluster), wine, leather/fashion, pharma/vaccine research (Siena)
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: distinct Tuscan identity and the historical origin of standard Italian, no separatism

autarky.rationale: Chianti/Maremma agriculture and viticulture support strong food self-sufficiency; Prato's textile district gives above-average clothing self-sufficiency relative to most other Italian regions in this dataset.

rationales.water: Arno-basin and Apennine supply is generally reliable outside drought years.
rationales.food: Chianti/Maremma viticulture and agriculture give strong self-sufficiency.
rationales.energy: Larderello geothermal field gives Tuscany a genuine (if regionally concentrated) domestic generation source.

sources: Tuscan Renaissance and dialect-standardization literature (Bembo's codification of Tuscan)

parliament.name: Consiglio regionale della Toscana
parliament.note: Italian region with its own Consiglio regionale (regional council/parliament).

regions.name: Umbria
regions.identity_basis: Italy's only landlocked peninsular region south of the Alps, self-styled 'the green heart of Italy'; distinct Umbrian identity predating Roman conquest (ancient Umbri people); assessed and retained per inclusion test.
regions.population_note: Eurostat 2023 estimate (ISTAT), Umbria NUTS-2 ITI2

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Perugia — regional capital, university city (Università per Stranieri), chocolate-industry headquarters
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: steel manufacturing (Terni), confectionery (Perugina/Nestlé), olive oil and Sagrantino wine, pilgrimage/cultural tourism (Assisi)
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: distinct pre-Roman Umbrian identity and 'green heart of Italy' self-image, no separatism; assessed against the inclusion test and retained as a clear pass

autarky.rationale: Landlocked but water-rich (Alpine-fed rivers, Trasimeno basin) with strong olive-oil/wine agriculture; smaller scale and hillier terrain than Tuscany moderate transportation and industrial-diversification scores slightly.

rationales.water: Landlocked but water-rich via Alpine-fed rivers and the Trasimeno basin.
rationales.food: Olive oil and Sagrantino-wine agriculture support strong self-sufficiency for a small region.
rationales.energy: No major domestic generation source; net importer via the national grid.

parliament.name: Consiglio regionale dell'Umbria
parliament.note: Italian region with its own Consiglio regionale (regional council/parliament).

regions.name: Marche
regions.identity_basis: Adriatic-facing region named for the medieval marches (border marks) of the Holy Roman Empire; distinctive dense small-and-medium-enterprise manufacturing model ('Marche model') and its own dialect continuum; assessed and retained per inclusion test.
regions.population_note: Eurostat 2023 estimate (ISTAT), Marche NUTS-2 ITI3

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Ancona — regional capital and Adriatic port; polycentric SME network across Pesaro/Fermo/Ascoli distinctive of the region
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: footwear/leather manufacturing district (among Italy's largest), furniture, musical instruments, agri-food
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: distinct Marche regional identity and dense SME industrial model, no separatism; assessed against the inclusion test and retained given its genuinely diversified manufacturing base

autarky.rationale: Dense small-manufacturing base (footwear, furniture) gives above-average clothing/shelter-input self-sufficiency for the dataset; moderate agriculture supports food self-sufficiency without regional standout strength.

rationales.water: Adriatic-slope rivers give adequate, unremarkable supply.
rationales.food: Moderate agri-food output; not a regional standout either way.
rationales.energy: Dense SME manufacturing (footwear, furniture) draws on grid power with little domestic generation.

parliament.name: Consiglio regionale delle Marche
parliament.note: Italian region with its own Consiglio regionale (regional council/parliament).

regions.name: Lazio (Rome)
regions.identity_basis: Region of the Italian and Vatican capital; Roman identity as ancient imperial and modern national capital, distinct from surrounding regions per its unique administrative-political centrality (analogous to the Madrid-region logic).
regions.population_note: Eurostat 2023 estimate (ISTAT), Lazio NUTS-2 ITI4

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Rome — metro ~4.3M, national capital, seat of the Vatican (independent enclave, not included in this record's geometry)
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: public administration, film/media (Cinecittà studios), pharma, aerospace/ICT, tourism
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: capital-region identity analogous to Madrid; no separatism

autarky.rationale: Best transport connectivity in central Italy as capital region; food and energy self-sufficiency are moderate, constrained by the demands of a large, mostly service-economy metropolis.

rationales.water: Tiber-basin reservoirs meet normal demand but leave little margin for a large capital-region population.
rationales.food: Moderate, constrained by the demands of a large, mostly service-economy metropolis.
rationales.energy: No significant domestic generation for the capital region; grid-imported power dominates.

reach.note: Rome's metropolitan labor market and service catchment extends into neighboring regions' bordering provinces.

parliament.name: Consiglio regionale del Lazio
parliament.note: Italian region with its own Consiglio regionale (regional council/parliament).

regions.name: Abruzzo
regions.identity_basis: Mountainous Apennine region (Gran Sasso, Majella national parks) historically administered jointly with Molise as 'Abruzzi e Molise' until their formal separation in 1963; Molise (ITF2) folded back into this record given Molise's very small population (~290,000) and its own weak independent urban hub, per the assess-and-merge instruction rather than treating it as a standalone region.
key_industries: automotive supply (Honda/Fiat components, Val di Sangro)
regions.population_note: Eurostat/ISTAT 2023 estimate, sum of Abruzzo (ITF1, ~1,275,000) and Molise (ITF2, ~290,000)

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Pescara — largest Abruzzese urban center on the Adriatic coast; L'Aquila as historic regional capital (post-2009 earthquake reconstruction hub)
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: automotive-parts manufacturing (Val di Sangro cluster), biomedical research, saffron/wine agriculture, national-park tourism
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: distinct Abruzzese mountain identity; Molise assessed independently and found too small/weak-hubbed to pass the inclusion test alone, merged here reflecting its pre-1963 administrative union with Abruzzo

autarky.rationale: Apennine watershed gives strong water self-sufficiency; automotive-parts and biomedical manufacturing provide moderate industrial diversification, though the region (especially Molise) remains one of Italy's less economically dense.

rationales.water: Apennine watershed (Gran Sasso, Majella) gives strong water self-sufficiency.
rationales.food: Saffron/wine agriculture on Apennine slopes gives moderate self-sufficiency.
rationales.energy: Limited domestic generation; automotive-parts manufacturing (Val di Sangro) draws on the grid.

pole.note: L'Aquila is the regional capital; Pescara is the larger, economically dominant coastal city.

parliament.name: Consiglio regionale dell'Abruzzo
parliament.note: Italian region with its own Consiglio regionale (regional council/parliament).

regions.name: Campania (Naples)
regions.identity_basis: Historic Kingdom of Naples/Two Sicilies capital region; distinctive Neapolitan language, cuisine (pizza's origin), and dense urban-agricultural identity; Italy's third most populous region.
key_industries: agri-food (San Marzano tomatoes, mozzarella di bufala)
regions.population_note: Eurostat 2023 estimate (ISTAT), Campania NUTS-2 ITF3

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Naples — metro ~3M, historic Kingdom of Naples capital and one of Italy's largest ports
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: aerospace manufacturing, PDO agri-food (San Marzano tomato, buffalo mozzarella), globally iconic tourism (Amalfi Coast, Pompeii), port logistics
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: strong distinct Neapolitan linguistic-cultural identity, no separatism

autarky.rationale: Volcanic-soil (Vesuvian) agriculture gives strong food self-sufficiency; dense urban informality and infrastructure strain (waste management, southern-Italy healthcare gaps) weigh down shelter and hygiene-healthcare scores.

rationales.water: Volcanic (Vesuvian) aquifers are fertile but dense urban Naples strains supply infrastructure.
rationales.food: Volcanic-soil agriculture (San Marzano tomato, buffalo mozzarella) gives strong food self-sufficiency.
rationales.energy: No major domestic generation; dense urban demand nets an importer.

sources: Kingdom of Naples/Two Sicilies historical-identity literature

parliament.name: Consiglio regionale della Campania
parliament.note: Italian region with its own Consiglio regionale (regional council/parliament).

regions.name: Puglia (Bari)
regions.identity_basis: Distinct heel-of-Italy identity (Salento sub-identity in the deep south, Griko Greek-speaking minority villages); mandated standalone per global constraints (Puglia≠Campania).
regions.population_note: Eurostat 2023 estimate (ISTAT), Puglia NUTS-2 ITF4

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Bari — metro ~1M, Adriatic port and university city
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: olive-oil/wine agriculture (one of Italy's top producers), Taranto steelworks, aerospace composites manufacturing, Salento tourism
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: distinct Apulian and, in the Salento, Griko-Greek minority identity, mandated separation from Campania per project brief

autarky.rationale: Among Italy's leading olive-oil and wine producers, giving very high food self-sufficiency; water stress (limited natural aquifers, agricultural over-extraction) is the clear binding constraint.

rationales.water: Limited natural aquifers and agricultural over-extraction make water the clear binding constraint.
rationales.food: Among Italy's leading olive-oil and wine producers, giving very high food self-sufficiency.
rationales.energy: Taranto steelworks and Gioia Tauro-adjacent industry are energy-intensive; solar buildout only partly offsets this.

parliament.name: Consiglio regionale della Puglia
parliament.note: Italian region with its own Consiglio regionale (regional council/parliament).

regions.name: Calabria
regions.identity_basis: Southernmost mainland Italian region (the 'toe'); distinct Calabrese identity with Griko/Arbëreshë (Albanian) minority pockets; retained standalone despite a genuinely weak, polycentric urban-hub profile, per the 'challenge rather than silently drop' instruction.
key_industries: agri-food (bergamot — near-global monopoly, olive oil, citrus)
regions.population_note: Eurostat 2023 estimate (ISTAT), Calabria NUTS-2 ITF6

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Reggio Calabria — largest city (~180k) and regional cultural anchor, though Calabria is unusually polycentric (Catanzaro is the administrative capital, Cosenza the university city) with no single dominant metro; flagged as the weakest urban-hub fit in this zone rather than silently merged elsewhere, since no adjacent region is a culturally honest merge target
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: near-global monopoly on bergamot essential oil, Gioia Tauro (one of the Mediterranean's largest transshipment ports), citrus/olive agriculture, fishing; legitimate industrial diversification is constrained by organized-crime ('Ndrangheta) economic distortion, noted honestly
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: strong distinct Calabrese identity with Griko and Arbëreshë linguistic minority enclaves, no separatism

autarky.rationale: Bergamot, citrus, and olive agriculture give solid food self-sufficiency; the region has Italy's lowest healthcare/hygiene infrastructure indicators and weakest formal industrial base, reflecting persistent southern-Italy development gaps compounded by organized-crime economic distortion.

rationales.water: Apennine/coastal rivers give adequate raw supply though distribution infrastructure lags.
rationales.food: Bergamot, citrus, and olive agriculture give solid self-sufficiency.
rationales.energy: No significant domestic generation; Italy's weakest formal industrial base limits energy self-sufficiency generally.

pole.note: Catanzaro is the official regional capital; Reggio Calabria the largest city, Cosenza the university city — a documented three-way polycentric triad (see zone notes).

parliament.name: Consiglio regionale della Calabria
parliament.note: Italian region with its own Consiglio regionale (regional council/parliament).

regions.name: Sicily
regions.identity_basis: Mediterranean's largest island, special-statute autonomous region with a distinct Sicilian language, layered Greek-Arab-Norman cultural history, and a historic (though not currently active) independentist movement (MIS, 1943-46).
regions.population_note: Eurostat 2023 estimate (ISTAT), Sicilia NUTS-2 ITG1

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Palermo — metro ~1.2M, historic Greek-Arab-Norman capital and special-statute regional seat; Catania as secondary tech/logistics hub (Etna Valley)
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: citrus/wine agriculture, one of Europe's largest petrochemical complexes (Syracuse-Augusta-Priolo), globally iconic archaeological tourism, growing solar-energy sector
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: special-statute autonomy, distinct Sicilian language and layered Mediterranean identity, historic but dormant independentism

autarky.rationale: Chronic water stress and periodic drought/reservoir shortfalls (worsened 2023-24) are the clear binding constraint despite strong citrus and viticulture output and good solar-energy potential.

rationales.water: Chronic drought and reservoir shortfalls (worsened 2023-24) are the clear binding constraint.
rationales.food: Citrus and viticulture output is strong despite the water stress.
rationales.energy: Growing solar sector plus Syracuse-Augusta refining capacity give above-average generation for the Italian south.

pole.note: Palermo: special-statute regional capital; Catania: comparable economic/tech weight (Etna Valley) — well-documented rivalry.

parliament.name: Assemblea Regionale Siciliana
parliament.note: Italian region with its own Consiglio regionale (regional council/parliament). Special-statute region (regione a statuto speciale) with enhanced legislative competencies.

regions.name: Sardinia
regions.identity_basis: Special-statute autonomous island region with the Sardinian language (linguistically the most distinct Romance language from standard Italian) and a small but persistent independentist current; culturally and geographically distinct from Sicily and the mainland.
regions.population_note: Eurostat 2023 estimate (ISTAT), Sardegna NUTS-2 ITG2

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Cagliari — metro ~430k, regional capital and special-statute seat
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: petrochemical refining, luxury tourism (Costa Smeralda), historic mining legacy, sheep-dairy (Pecorino Sardo/Romano) agri-food, wind/solar energy
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: distinct Sardinian language and identity, special-statute autonomy, small persistent independentist movement (Sardigna Natzione) but not currently a governing force

autarky.rationale: Pastoral sheep-dairy economy gives strong food self-sufficiency and good wind/solar energy potential; island transportation dependence on ferry/air links to the mainland is the clear structural constraint.

rationales.water: Adequate but seasonally stressed by tourism demand on the Costa Smeralda coast.
rationales.food: Pastoral sheep-dairy economy (Pecorino) gives strong food self-sufficiency.
rationales.energy: Wind/solar potential is good and Sarroch refining adds capacity, but island transport dependence remains the bigger constraint.

parliament.name: Consiglio regionale della Sardegna
parliament.note: Italian region with its own Consiglio regionale (regional council/parliament). Special-statute region (regione a statuto speciale) with enhanced legislative competencies.

regions.name: La Rioja
regions.identity_basis: Small Ebro-valley Autonomous Community with a distinct Riojan wine-region identity and its own (contested) claim to early Castilian-language origins (Glosas Emilianenses, San Millán de la Cogolla monastery); split from the old NUTS-1 Noreste bloc as its own unit in schema v2 to close a coverage hole flagged in v1.
regions.population_note: Eurostat 2023 estimate (INE), La Rioja NUTS-2 ES23

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Logroño — regional capital and center of the DOCa Rioja wine trade
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: world-renowned Rioja wine appellation, footwear manufacturing (Arnedo), agri-food canning
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: distinct Riojan wine-culture identity within Spain, historic claim as cradle of written Castilian; too small alone for a full-weight representation seat (population ~319,000), grouped with Basque Country + Aragón at the representation layer

parliament.name: Parlamento de La Rioja
parliament.note: Spanish Autonomous Community with its own Statute of Autonomy and unicameral parliament.

autarky.rationale: Dense, high-value viticulture gives strong food/wine self-sufficiency for a very small territory; footwear manufacturing lifts clothing above the Spanish-region average.

rationales.water: Ebro-valley irrigation is reliable for a small, densely cultivated territory.
rationales.food: Dense, high-value Rioja viticulture gives very high food/wine self-sufficiency relative to population.
rationales.energy: No significant domestic generation; small territory relies on the wider Spanish grid.

sources: IER (Instituto de Estadística de La Rioja)

regions.name: Cantabria
regions.identity_basis: Small Atlantic-coast Autonomous Community with a distinct Cantabrian (Montañés) identity and dialect substrate, historically part of 'Old Castile' before its 1981 statute of autonomy; closes a coverage hole flagged in v1.
regions.population_note: Eurostat 2023 estimate (ICANE), Cantabria NUTS-2 ES13

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Santander — regional capital and Atlantic port, Menéndez Pelayo/UIMP cultural anchor
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: port logistics, legacy steel/metallurgy, dairy-pasture agriculture, coastal tourism
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: distinct Cantabrian coastal identity, no separatism; small population makes it too weak for a full-weight standalone representation seat, grouped with Asturias+Galicia at the representation layer

parliament.name: Parlamento de Cantabria
parliament.note: Spanish Autonomous Community with its own Statute of Autonomy and unicameral parliament.

autarky.rationale: Atlantic rainfall and dairy pasture give solid water/food scores; legacy heavy industry has declined without full replacement, capping energy and clothing self-sufficiency.

rationales.water: Atlantic rainfall gives ample, reliable supply.
rationales.food: Dairy-pasture agriculture supports moderate self-sufficiency.
rationales.energy: Declining legacy heavy industry (steel) leaves limited domestic generation to offset demand.

regions.name: Asturias
regions.identity_basis: Distinct Astur-Leonese linguistic identity (Asturian/Bable, with regional co-official protection) and a historic Principality title; Spain's post-industrial heavy-industry heartland (Gijón/Avilés steel and coal); closes a coverage hole flagged in v1.
regions.population_note: Eurostat 2023 estimate (SADEI), Principado de Asturias NUTS-2 ES12

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Oviedo (political capital) / Gijón (largest city, port and industrial hub) — polycentric 'Asturias central' conurbation
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: steel and heavy industry (ArcelorMittal), port logistics, dairy/cider agri-food, mountain and coastal tourism
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: distinct Asturian (Bable) language with regional protection, historic Principality of Asturias title, no separatism

parliament.name: Junta General del Principado de Asturias
parliament.note: Spanish Autonomous Community with its own Statute of Autonomy and unicameral parliament.

autarky.rationale: Atlantic rainfall and pasture-based dairy/cider agriculture give strong water/food scores; post-industrial decline in steel/coal has not been fully replaced, moderating energy and clothing self-sufficiency.

rationales.water: Atlantic rainfall and mountain catchments give strong, reliable supply.
rationales.food: Dairy/cider agriculture on Atlantic pasture gives solid self-sufficiency.
rationales.energy: Post-industrial decline of coal/steel has not been fully replaced by renewables; moderate score.

sources: SADEI (Sociedad Asturiana de Estudios Económicos e Industriales)

regions.name: Extremadura
regions.identity_basis: Historic western-border Autonomous Community with a distinct Extremaduran identity and residual Estremeñu (Astur-Leonese-family) dialect; one of Spain's poorest regions by GDP per capita, with a genuine rural-agrarian identity; closes a coverage hole flagged in v1.
regions.population_note: Eurostat 2023 estimate (IEEX), Extremadura NUTS-2 ES43

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Mérida (regional capital, UNESCO Roman-heritage city) / Badajoz (largest city, cross-border hub with Portugal)
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: dehesa Iberian-ham pastoralism, tobacco and cherry agriculture, leading solar-power generation capacity, Roman-heritage tourism
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: distinct Extremaduran regional identity and residual Estremeñu dialect, no separatism

pole.note: Mérida is the seat of regional government; Badajoz is the larger city and cross-border hub with Portugal (Elvas).

parliament.name: Asamblea de Extremadura
parliament.note: Spanish Autonomous Community with its own Statute of Autonomy and unicameral parliament.

autarky.rationale: Dehesa pastoralism and leading Spanish solar-power capacity give very high food/energy scores; sparse population and peripheral position give the weakest transport/healthcare infrastructure scores of the new Spanish units.

rationales.water: Guadiana-basin reservoirs are adequate for a sparsely populated region despite periodic drought.
rationales.food: Dehesa Iberian-ham pastoralism and cherry/tobacco agriculture give very high food self-sufficiency.
rationales.energy: Leading Spanish solar-power generation capacity gives an energy-positive position.

regions.name: Murcia
regions.identity_basis: Distinct Murcian identity and Panocho/Murciano dialect on the southeastern Mediterranean coast; a major intensive-agriculture export economy ('Europe's orchard'); closes a coverage hole flagged in v1.
regions.population_note: Eurostat 2023 estimate (CREM), Región de Murcia NUTS-2 ES62

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Murcia — metro ~700k, regional capital and university city; Cartagena as historic naval/port hub
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: intensive horticultural export agriculture, Cartagena naval/commercial port and petrochemicals, growing solar/wind energy
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: distinct Murcian (Panocho) identity, no separatism

parliament.name: Asamblea Regional de Murcia
parliament.note: Spanish Autonomous Community with its own Statute of Autonomy and unicameral parliament.

autarky.rationale: Structural water scarcity (Tagus-Segura transfer dependence, Mar Menor eutrophication crisis) is the region's binding constraint despite very high horticultural export output and strong solar potential.

rationales.water: Structural scarcity (Tagus-Segura transfer dependence, Mar Menor crisis) is the region's clear binding constraint.
rationales.food: Intensive horticultural export agriculture ('Europe's orchard') gives very high output despite the water stress.
rationales.energy: Strong solar/wind buildout gives above-average generation capacity.

sources: CREM (Centro Regional de Estadística de Murcia)

regions.special_status: Spanish exclaves on the North African coast; discontiguous with mainland Spain; sovereignty disputed by Morocco.

conflict_flags.description: Morocco claims sovereignty over both Ceuta and Melilla as territories to be decolonized/reintegrated; Spain administers them as autonomous cities. Flagged, not adjudicated.

regions.name: Spanish North-African territories
regions.identity_basis: Two Spanish autonomous cities on the North African coast (Ceuta ES63, Melilla ES64), combined into one special-status unit per project mandate; each fails the independent-scale urban-hub and diversified-industry criteria comparable to the microstate exceptions, and both are geographically discontiguous exclaves rather than part of contiguous Iberia — the v1 reasoning for exclusion is preserved here, but schema v2 mandates a special_status unit rather than an outright drop, matching the dashed-border treatment given to Gibraltar, Vorarlberg, etc.
regions.population_note: Eurostat 2023 estimate (INE), sum of Ciudad de Ceuta (ES63, ~83,000) + Ciudad de Melilla (ES64, ~86,000)

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Ceuta and Melilla are each single-city exclaves with no independent metro area beyond their municipal footprint
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: cross-border land-customs trade with Morocco, fishing, public-administration/garrison employment; weak formal industrial diversification, comparable to the microstate exceptions
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: Spanish autonomous-city status, discontiguous exclave geography, live sovereignty dispute with Morocco

pole.note: Non-contiguous twin exclaves ~350km apart along the Moroccan coast; administratively equal, Ceuta listed first by convention (larger of the two land borders).

parliament.name: Asamblea de Ceuta + Asamblea de Melilla
parliament.note: Autonomous cities (not full Autonomous Communities); each has an Asamblea with more limited competencies than a Comunidad Autónoma parliament — borderline case, included per the parliament rule but flagged as a lesser degree of self-government.

autarky.rationale: Small, discontiguous exclaves with essentially no domestic agriculture, energy generation, or manufacturing base; near-total dependence on mainland Spain/Morocco supply lines gives the lowest composite score in this dataset.

rationales.water: No independent catchment of consequence; both exclaves depend on desalination/mainland supply.
rationales.food: Essentially no domestic agriculture; near-total import dependence across the land border with Morocco or by sea.
rationales.energy: No domestic generation; entirely grid/fuel-import dependent for two small enclave cities.

regions.special_status: British Overseas Territory on the southern tip of Iberia; sovereignty disputed by Spain; distinct micro-jurisdiction with own Parliament, legal system, and currency.

conflict_flags.description: Spain claims sovereignty over Gibraltar (ceded to Britain in perpetuity under the 1713 Treaty of Utrecht, but Spain disputes this); Gibraltarians have twice rejected shared/Spanish sovereignty by referendum (1967, 2002). Flagged, not adjudicated.

regions.name: Gibraltar
regions.identity_basis: British Overseas Territory (population ~32,700) at the southern tip of the Iberian Peninsula; distinct Llanito (English-Spanish code-switching) vernacular culture; self-governing with its own Parliament since 1969/2006 Constitution; a live sovereignty dispute with Spain (referenda 1967/2002 both rejected Spanish sovereignty or shared sovereignty). Geometry sourced from the CNTR file (CNTR_ID 'GI'); no NUTS code exists for Gibraltar since it is not a Spanish or EU-NUTS unit — resolved without needing the UK NUTS2021 fallback path.
regions.population_note: 2023 Gibraltar Government census estimate

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Gibraltar (the entire territory is effectively a single dense urban settlement around the Rock)
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: financial services and online gaming (major revenue base), port bunkering/ship supply, tourism, shipping registry
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: self-governing British Overseas Territory, distinct Llanito culture, historically dependent on the UK rather than seeking independence; live sovereignty dispute with Spain kept as context, not adjudicated

parliament.name: Parliament of Gibraltar
parliament.note: British Overseas Territory with its own directly-elected 17-member Parliament and Government under the 2006 Constitution.

autarky.rationale: A 6.7 km² territory with essentially no domestic agriculture, energy generation, or manufacturing; near-total dependence on imports across the land border with Spain and by sea gives the lowest food/energy/clothing scores in the dataset alongside Ceuta-Melilla.

rationales.water: No natural freshwater source of consequence; historically reliant on rock-catchment cisterns, now desalination.
rationales.food: No domestic agriculture on a 6.7 km² territory; entirely import-dependent across the land border with Spain.
rationales.energy: No domestic generation; imported fuel/grid power for the entire territory.

regions.name: Basilicata
regions.identity_basis: Southern Italian region (historically Lucania) between Campania, Puglia, and Calabria; Matera's Sassi UNESCO district and its 2019 European Capital of Culture status give it a genuine urban-cultural hub despite the region's small population; v1 explicitly flagged this region as 'a strong candidate for inclusion' and it is added here to close a coverage hole and satisfy the schema v2 blocking coverage test.
key_industries: oil/gas extraction (Val d'Agri, Italy's largest onshore field)
regions.population_note: Eurostat 2023 estimate (ISTAT), Basilicata NUTS-2 ITF5

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Matera — UNESCO World Heritage Sassi district, 2019 European Capital of Culture; Potenza as regional political capital
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: Val d'Agri onshore oil/gas field (Italy's largest), Stellantis automotive assembly (Melfi), viticulture/olive-oil agri-food, cultural tourism
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: distinct Lucanian regional identity, own regional government, no separatism

pole.note: Potenza is the political capital; Matera is the internationally recognized cultural hub (2019 ECoC).

parliament.name: Consiglio regionale della Basilicata
parliament.note: Italian region with its own Consiglio regionale (regional council/parliament).

autarky.rationale: Domestic oil/gas extraction gives an unusually high energy score for a small southern Italian region; mountainous, sparsely connected terrain and thin healthcare infrastructure are the binding constraints, similar to Calabria.

rationales.water: Apennine headwaters (including the Pertusillo reservoir) give adequate supply for a low-density region.
rationales.food: Viticulture and olive-oil agriculture give solid self-sufficiency.
rationales.energy: The Val d'Agri field (Italy's largest onshore oil/gas deposit) gives Basilicata an unusually energy-positive position for its size.

sources: Matera 2019 European Capital of Culture documentation

regions.name: Alentejo
regions.identity_basis: Vast, sparsely populated rural-agrarian region south and east of the Tagus; distinct Alentejano identity (cante alentejano UNESCO-listed polyphonic singing, cork/wine dehesa-style latifundio economy); v1 explicitly assessed and left this out for a weak urban hub (Évora under 55,000). Authored as its OWN unit here rather than extending Lisbon southward: identity-true reasoning holds that Alentejo's rural-agrarian, cork/wine cultural character is genuinely distinct from capital-region Lisbon, and stretching Lisbon's cultural unit over it would misrepresent the region rather than honestly reflect a weak-but-real identity (same standard as Calabria/Algarve treatment in v1). Alentejo IS folded into Lisbon at the representation (groupings) layer, which addresses the 'Lisbon cover the south' administrative-gravity argument without flattening the cultural map.
regions.population_note: Approximate 2023 estimate; Portugal's 2024 NUTS-2 boundary revision changed Alentejo's exact composition (Lezíria do Tejo moved to Oeste e Vale do Tejo) — figure not independently reconciled against a post-revision Eurostat table in this pass, flagged for verification.

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Évora — UNESCO World Heritage city and regional cultural capital, though under 55,000 population — the weakest urban-hub fit added in this wave, flagged honestly rather than silently merged
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: world's largest cork-producing region, Alentejo DOC wine, extensive livestock/cereal agriculture, leading solar-power generation capacity
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: distinct Alentejano rural identity (UNESCO-listed cante alentejano singing tradition), no separatism; added for coverage and identity reasons, folded into Lisbon at the representation layer only

parliament.note: Mainland Portugal unitary structure — no regional parliament; unit added purely for coverage (blocking coverage-test gap) and Alentejo's distinct rural-agrarian identity.

autarky.rationale: Extensive dehesa-style agriculture (cork, wine, livestock) and leading solar-power capacity give very high food/energy scores; Portugal's most sparsely populated mainland region has the thinnest healthcare/transport infrastructure and virtually no clothing/textile manufacturing base.

rationales.water: Alqueva reservoir (Europe's largest artificial lake) gives strong irrigation and drinking-water capacity.
rationales.food: Extensive dehesa-style cork/wine/livestock agriculture gives very high food self-sufficiency.
rationales.energy: Leading Portuguese solar-power generation capacity gives an energy-positive position.

regions.name: Centro
regions.identity_basis: Central mainland Portuguese NUTS-2 unit between Porto/Norte and Lisbon; Coimbra's university (Portugal's oldest, founded 1290, UNESCO World Heritage) is a real cultural hub, though v1 assessed the surrounding NUTS-2 aggregation as lacking Porto/Norte's unified regional identity. Authored here as its own unit purely to close a blocking coverage-test gap (Centro is the largest of the three previously-uncovered mainland Portuguese NUTS-2 areas); its comparatively diffuse, polycentric character (Coimbra/Aveiro/Viseu/Leiria, no single dominant city) is stated honestly rather than invented.
regions.population_note: Approximate 2023-era estimate under pre-2024 Centro boundaries; the 2024 NUTS-2 revision changed composition (absorbing/losing units versus the prior Região Centro) — figure not independently reconciled against a post-revision Eurostat table in this pass, flagged for verification.

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Coimbra — Portugal's oldest university (1290), UNESCO World Heritage city; genuinely polycentric alongside Aveiro/Viseu/Leiria with no single dominant metro
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: university/research economy, ceramics and glass manufacturing (Marinha Grande crystal, Aveiro), forestry/paper-pulp, Bairrada wine agriculture
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: real but diffuse regional identity compared to Porto/Norte's; added primarily to close the mainland-Portugal coverage gap rather than on a strong independent-identity claim, stated honestly

parliament.note: Mainland Portugal unitary structure — no regional parliament; unit added purely for coverage (blocking coverage-test gap); Coimbra university-city identity is real but comparatively diffuse across the NUTS-2 unit.

autarky.rationale: Atlantic-facing agriculture/forestry and a diversified manufacturing base (ceramics, glass, paper) give solid, unremarkable-but-adequate scores across most dimensions, consistent with the region's real character as a productive but less internationally distinctive part of mainland Portugal.

rationales.water: Atlantic-facing river basins (Mondego, Vouga) give reliable, unremarkable supply.
rationales.food: Forestry, Bairrada viticulture, and mixed agriculture give solid self-sufficiency.
rationales.energy: No major domestic generation; ceramics/glass/paper manufacturing draws on the national grid.

sources: University of Coimbra UNESCO inscription documentation

conflict_flags.description: Historically, Comunidad de Madrid was carved out of 'New Castile'/La Mancha territory (formalized 1833, autonomous community 1983). This composite deliberately excludes Madrid to preserve the site's Catalonia-Madrid flagship framing; a historically 'fuller' Castile would include it. Flagged rather than silently resolved.

regions.name: Greater Castile (unified)
regions.identity_basis: Non-congruent composite union of León(Castile) + La Mancha(Castile) — i.e. the historic 'Old Castile' (Castilla la Vieja, NUTS-2 ES41) plus 'New Castile' (Castilla la Nueva, NUTS-2 ES42) — representing the pre-1833-provincial-reform, pre-Madrid-secession idea of a single Castilian cultural bloc. Comunidad de Madrid (ES30) is DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED even though it was historically carved out of New Castile/La Mancha in 1833: Madrid is authored as its own flagship capital-region unit (monopole, site-framing counterweight to Catalonia) and reuniting it here would contradict that mandate and the map's Catalonia-Madrid tension example. This is the 'connected' view of the leon-castile variant set.
regions.population_note: Sum of es-castile-leon (ES41, ~2,383,000) + es-castile-la-mancha (ES42, ~2,050,000); non-default composite, Madrid (ES30) deliberately excluded.

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Valladolid (largest city of the union) — no single unified capital exists for this composite
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: combined cereal/wine agriculture, automotive manufacturing across both member territories
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: represents a historical pan-Castilian identity frame rather than a governing reality; both member Autonomous Communities retain their own separate statutes and parliaments

parliament.note: Non-governing composite; the two member Autonomous Communities each retain their own real parliament (Cortes de Castilla y León, Cortes de Castilla-La Mancha).

autarky.rationale: Combines two high-food-autarky cereal/wine plateaus; scores approximate the population-weighted average of the two member records.

rationales.water: Combines two plateau basins (Duero + Mancha aquifer); adequate on average though the Mancha side is structurally over-exploited.
rationales.food: Combines two of the dataset's highest-food-scoring records (cereal breadbasket + wine plain).
rationales.energy: Combines Castile-León's wind buildout with Castile-La Mancha's solar buildout for a solidly positive composite.

sources: Junta de Castilla y León statistical office
Instituto de Estadística de Castilla-La Mancha
1833 Javier de Burgos provincial-division historical literature

conflict_flags.description: Using full NUTS-3 provinces (Segovia, Ávila, Guadalajara, Toledo) rather than finer municipal/comarca geometry means this record includes large rural areas of each province far outside any realistic daily-commute shed of Madrid. No finer NUTS geometry is available in the index; flagged rather than silently corrected, matching the existing basque-unified/FRI15 precedent.

regions.name: Madrid & Surroundings
regions.identity_basis: Extended commuter-belt variant of Madrid, reaching into the nearest NUTS-3 provinces of both neighboring Castiles that function as Madrid's daily-commuter/exurban catchment: Segovia (ES416) and Ávila (ES411) from Castile-León to the northwest, Guadalajara (ES424) and Toledo (ES425) from Castile-La Mancha to the east/south. Codes are deliberately at NUTS-3 (province) granularity, not the coarser NUTS-2 Autonomous Community level, to avoid grossly overstating the commuter belt by annexing entire neighboring regions. This is the 'with-surroundings' view of the madrid variant set.
regions.population_note: Comunidad de Madrid (ES300, ~6,751,000) + approximate combined population of the four bordering commuter-belt NUTS-3 provinces (Segovia+Ávila+Guadalajara+Toledo, order-of-magnitude ~150,000-800,000 depending on how much of each large, mostly-rural province is actually within Madrid's functional commute-shed; not independently reconciled against province-level Eurostat tables in this pass, flagged for verification).

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Madrid — same national-capital hub as the congruent es-madrid record
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: same as es-madrid, plus the surrounding provinces' logistics/warehousing and agri-food capacity
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: functional commuter-belt extension, not a distinct identity claim; represents Madrid's real metropolitan-region gravity beyond the Comunidad de Madrid's own administrative boundary

parliament.note: Non-governing composite; Madrid retains its own Asamblea, the bordering provinces belong to Castile-León/Castile-La Mancha's respective parliaments.

autarky.rationale: Adding four largely rural/agricultural provinces to Madrid's core slightly raises food self-sufficiency relative to the congruent record; transport/healthcare remain capital-region-dominated scores.

rationales.water: Adds four largely rural provinces' catchments to Madrid's reservoir system; modest net improvement.
rationales.food: Adding rural/agricultural provinces slightly raises food self-sufficiency relative to the congruent Madrid record.
rationales.energy: Still dominated by Madrid's own import-dependent profile; the added provinces contribute little generation capacity.

sources: Comunidad de Madrid regional statistics office

regions.name: Helsinki-Uusimaa
regions.identity_basis: Finland's capital region and its southeastern hinterland (Kanta-Häme, Päijät-Häme, Kymenlaakso, Etelä-Karjala); bilingual Finnish/Swedish administrative and cultural core distinct from the western and eastern-Finnish dialect areas.
regions.population_note: Statistics Finland 2023 estimate, sum of Helsinki-Uusimaa (FI1B1) plus Kanta-Häme, Etelä-Karjala, Päijät-Häme and Kymenlaakso (FI1C2/5/6/7)

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Helsinki metro >1.5M; national government, Nokia/ICT cluster, University of Helsinki
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: software and telecoms, finance/insurance, container/energy port at Kotka-Hamina, cross-border trade with Russia (historically) via Lappeenranta/Imatra
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: strong capital-region identity and southeastern border-province identity within Finland; no separatism

regions.nuts1_disagreement: NUTS-1 FI1 (Manner-Suomi) treats all mainland Finland as one unit; split here into five Finnish nodes (Helsinki, Turku, Tampere/Western Finland, Oulu, Lapland/Sápmi) per the zone mandate, with Kanta-Häme/Päijät-Häme/Kymenlaakso/Etelä-Karjala (NUTS-2 FI1C minus Varsinais-Suomi) grouped into the Helsinki commuter/functional region rather than left as an unassigned residual.

autarky.rationale: Dense transport/health infrastructure and strong service economy; food and energy depend heavily on the rest of Finland and imports, offset partly by Kymenlaakso's agriculture and Kotka-Hamina's energy-import terminal.

rationales.water: Lake- and groundwater-fed supply from the southern Finnish moraine belt is ample.
rationales.food: Kymenlaakso agriculture is real but the capital-region population outstrips it; net food-import-dependent overall.
rationales.energy: Grid- and gas-import-dependent as a dense capital region; Kotka-Hamina's energy-import terminal underlines this rather than offsetting it.

sources: Helsinki-Uusimaa Regional Council (Uudenmaan liitto) statistical yearbook

pole.note: Helsinki overwhelmingly dominates its southeastern hinterland.

parliament.name: n/a
parliament.note: Finland is a unitary state; no regional parliament below the national Eduskunta. This region has an elected regional council (maakuntavaltuusto) with limited planning/healthcare powers, not a legislative parliament.

regions.name: Turku / Southwest Finland
regions.identity_basis: Finland's oldest urban settlement area and former capital; distinct Southwest-Finnish coastal identity with historic Swedish-speaking minority presence in the archipelago.
regions.population_note: Statistics Finland 2023 estimate, Varsinais-Suomi (FI1C1)

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Turku metro ~330,000; former national capital, Turku Castle/Cathedral, university city
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: cruise-ship building at Meyer Turku, biotech/pharma cluster, some of Finland's best arable farmland, Baltic ferry logistics
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: distinct Southwest-Finnish/archipelago identity and bilingual heritage within Finland; no separatism

regions.nuts1_disagreement: NUTS-2 FI1C (Etelä-Suomi) groups Varsinais-Suomi with Kanta-Häme/Päijät-Häme/Kymenlaakso/Etelä-Karjala; split here so Turku stands as its own mandated node, with the remaining FI1C provinces folded into the Helsinki functional region.

autarky.rationale: Best agricultural land in Finland gives strong food self-sufficiency; shipbuilding and ferry logistics support transport, but energy is grid-imported and clothing manufacture is negligible.

rationales.water: Aura river and southwestern-archipelago groundwater are ample.
rationales.food: Some of Finland's best arable farmland; a genuine regional surplus.
rationales.energy: Grid-imported; no major domestic generation asset within the region.

sources: Regional Council of Southwest Finland (Varsinais-Suomen liitto)

pole.note: Turku is the clear urban hub of Varsinais-Suomi.

parliament.name: n/a
parliament.note: Finland is a unitary state; regional council (maakuntavaltuusto) only, not a parliament.

regions.name: Tampere & Western Finland
regions.identity_basis: Finland's second-largest urban region and its western-coast hinterland, including Swedish-speaking Ostrobothnia; historic industrial ('Manchester of the North') identity distinct from Helsinki and Turku.
regions.population_note: Statistics Finland 2023 estimate, sum of NUTS-2 FI19 (Länsi-Suomi: Pirkanmaa, Satakunta, Keski-Suomi, Etelä-Pohjanmaa, Pohjanmaa)

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Tampere metro ~400,000; historic industrial city, now ICT/games and university hub
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: engineering/machinery, energy (Olkiluoto NPP in Satakunta), agriculture and food processing in Ostrobothnia, forestry
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: strong regional pride ('Tampere spirit') and distinct Swedish-speaking Ostrobothnian coastal identity within Finland; no separatism

autarky.rationale: Olkiluoto nuclear plant (Satakunta) and Ostrobothnian farmland give this region unusually strong energy and food self-sufficiency for Finland; clothing manufacture remains negligible.

rationales.water: Kokemaenjoki/Tammerkoski river network is ample.
rationales.food: Ostrobothnian farmland gives above-average food production for Finland.
rationales.energy: Olkiluoto nuclear plant (Satakunta) gives this region an unusually strong domestic generation asset for Finland.

pole.note: Tampere is the largest city, but Vaasa/Seinaejoki (Ostrobothnia) remain genuine secondary poles.

parliament.name: n/a
parliament.note: Finland is a unitary state; regional council only, not a parliament.

regions.name: Oulu & North Ostrobothnia
regions.identity_basis: Northern Finland's largest city and its immediate hinterland (Kainuu, Central Ostrobothnia); tech-industry identity distinct from both southern Finland and Sámi Lapland to its north.
regions.population_note: Statistics Finland 2023 estimate, sum of Pohjois-Pohjanmaa (FI1D9), Kainuu (FI1D8) and Keski-Pohjanmaa (FI1D5)

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Oulu metro ~250,000; Finland's fastest-growing city, University of Oulu, major tech hub
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: health/mobile tech spun out of the Nokia era, mining and bioeconomy in Kainuu, agriculture in Central Ostrobothnia
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: distinct northern Finnish identity, proud of tech-hub status, within Finland; no separatism

regions.nuts1_disagreement: NUTS-2 FI1D (Pohjois- ja Itä-Suomi) also includes Lappi (split here as its own mandated Lapland/Sápmi node) and the eastern lakeland provinces (Etelä-Savo, Pohjois-Savo, Pohjois-Karjala), which are left as an unassigned coverage gap pending their own inclusion-test pass (see zone notes).

autarky.rationale: Solid hydro/grid access and forestry-based energy; food and transport are moderate given the region's size and dispersed population relative to southern Finland.

rationales.water: Oulujoki river/hydropower network and boreal groundwater are ample.
rationales.food: Central Ostrobothnian agriculture is modest relative to the region's size.
rationales.energy: Solid hydro/grid access and forestry-based biomass keep this mid-tier.

pole.note: Oulu is Northern Finland's dominant city and tech hub.

parliament.name: n/a
parliament.note: Finland is a unitary state; regional council only, not a parliament.

regions.name: Lapland / Sápmi
regions.identity_basis: Finland's Arctic north; home to the Finnish Sámi homeland (Sápmi), an Indigenous cross-border cultural area also spanning northern Sweden and Norway, distinct from both mainstream Finnish identity and southern administration.
regions.population_note: Statistics Finland 2023 estimate, Lappi (FI1D7)

conflict_flags.description: Sápmi, the Indigenous Sámi homeland, spans northern Finland, Sweden and Norway and is not congruent with any national or NUTS boundary. This overlay flags the cross-border cultural area without redrawing national region boundaries; it may overlap the nuts_codes of the Norrland, Tromsø/North and other neighboring regions.

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Rovaniemi ~65,000; administrative capital of Finnish Lapland and seat of the Sámi Parliament of Finland
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: Arctic tourism, reindeer husbandry, Kemijoki hydropower, mining, forestry
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: distinct Sámi Indigenous identity plus a broader Lappish regional identity, both dependent on rather than seeking independence from Finland

regions.nuts1_disagreement: NUTS-2 FI1D groups Lappi with Kainuu/Pohjois-Pohjanmaa (folded into the Oulu node here) and the eastern lakeland provinces; split out as its own mandated node reflecting the distinct Sámi/Arctic identity.

autarky.rationale: Abundant glacial/snowmelt water and strong Kemijoki hydropower; harsh climate and vast distances limit food production and transportation, while healthcare access is thinner than in southern Finland.

rationales.water: Abundant glacial/snowmelt water and strong Kemijoki hydropower.
rationales.food: Harsh Arctic climate limits food production to reindeer husbandry and small-scale farming; structurally low.
rationales.energy: Kemijoki hydropower cascade gives strong energy self-sufficiency for a sparsely populated region.

sources: Sámediggi (Sámi Parliament of Finland) — Sápmi boundary description

pole.note: Rovaniemi is the administrative capital of Finnish Lapland and seat of the Sami Parliament of Finland.

parliament.name: Saamelaiskaerajaet (Sami Parliament of Finland)
parliament.note: Finland is a unitary state with no regional parliament, but the Sami Parliament of Finland (seated in Inari/Rovaniemi) has real cultural-autonomy competence over Sami affairs within this region -- a genuine partial exception worth the audit's attention.

regions.name: Åland Islands
regions.identity_basis: Autonomous, monolingually Swedish-speaking archipelago province with its own parliament, flag and demilitarized status; explicitly mandated as a separate island unit distinct from Gotland.
regions.population_note: Statistics Finland / Government of Åland (ÅSUB) 2023 estimate

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Mariehamn ~11,700; seat of the autonomous Åland Parliament (Lagting) and shipping-registry hub
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: maritime shipping/ferry operations, tourism, fishing and small-scale agriculture
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: autonomous, Swedish-speaking, demilitarized province with a strong distinct identity, constitutionally dependent on Finland (not seeking independence)

autarky.rationale: Ferry-based transport and a small grid make Åland import-dependent for energy (submarine cable from Sweden/Finland); fishing and small farms support modest food self-sufficiency.

rationales.water: Small archipelago catchments are adequate for the small population.
rationales.food: Fishing and small-scale farming support modest food self-sufficiency.
rationales.energy: A small island grid is import-dependent via submarine cable from Sweden/Finland.

pole.note: Mariehamn is the sole town and seat of the autonomous Aland Parliament.

parliament.name: Alands lagting

regions.name: Finnish Lakeland (Savo-Karelia)
regions.identity_basis: Eastern Finnish lakeland provinces (Etelä-Savo, Pohjois-Savo, Pohjois-Karjala) sharing a Savo/Karelian dialect continuum and lake-district identity distinct from both southern (Helsinki-Uusimaa) and northern (Oulu) Finland; previously an unassigned coverage gap in this zone (see zone notes), now given its own inclusion-test pass.
regions.population_note: Statistics Finland 2023 estimate, sum of Etelä-Savo (FI1DA), Pohjois-Savo (FI1DB) and Pohjois-Karjala (FI1DC)

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Kuopio (~123,000) is the largest single city and regional cultural anchor, but the lakeland is genuinely polycentric: Jyväskylä (just outside this region, in neighbouring Länsi-Suomi) and Joensuu/Lappeenranta are comparably-sized secondary poles rather than clear satellites of Kuopio -- flagged as a weak single-hub fit, mirroring the Calabria precedent in zone 3 (retained standalone rather than silently merged, since no adjacent region is a culturally honest merge target for the Savo/Karelian dialect area).
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: forestry and bioeconomy (pulp/paper, wood products), agriculture, lake-district tourism, and a significant higher-education/research base (University of Eastern Finland, split across Kuopio and Joensuu campuses)
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: distinct Savo and Karelian dialect/identity area within Finland; no separatism, but a genuine cultural self-conception distinct from both Helsinki and Oulu

regions.nuts1_disagreement: NUTS-2 FI1D (Pohjois- ja Itä-Suomi) groups this lakeland area with Lappland/Sápmi (FI1D7) and Oulu/Kainuu/Central Ostrobothnia (FI1D9/FI1D8/FI1D5); split here into its own region on dialect and lake-district identity grounds, consistent with the zone's finer-than-NUTS-1 approach elsewhere.

autarky.rationale: Extensive hydropower access and forestry-derived biomass give strong energy self-sufficiency; the lake district's abundant fresh water is a genuine surplus resource. Food is moderate (agriculture present but not surplus-scale). Transportation lags due to a lake-fragmented geography and dispersed population outside Kuopio.

rationales.water: The lake district's abundant fresh water is a genuine surplus resource.
rationales.food: Agriculture present but not surplus-scale; moderate.
rationales.energy: Extensive hydropower access and forestry-derived biomass give strong energy self-sufficiency.

sources: University of Eastern Finland regional profile

pole.note: Genuinely polycentric per the region's own inclusion-test note; Kuopio is the largest single anchor.

inclusion_test.dependent_identity: clear Stockholm-region identity within Sweden; strong commuter integration with Mälardalen towns, no separatism

rationales.water: Lake Malaren and its river network give abundant supply.
rationales.food: Food security depends on the wider Malardalen agricultural plain rather than the capital itself; moderate.
rationales.energy: Grid access to national hydro/nuclear supports energy, though the capital's demand keeps this mid-tier.

parliament.name: n/a
parliament.note: Sweden is a unitary state; the region has an elected regional council (regionfullmaktige, mainly healthcare/transit competence), not a legislative parliament.

regions.name: Gothenburg & West Sweden
regions.identity_basis: Sweden's second city and west-coast maritime/industrial region, extended here to include the inland Småland provinces (Jönköping, Kronoberg, Kalmar) that share West Sweden's functional-economic orbit and lack a separately mandated node.

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Gothenburg metro >1M; Scandinavia's largest port, Volvo headquarters
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: automotive manufacturing, maritime logistics, textile/design cluster (Borås), Småland furniture and glassworks industry
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: distinct West-Swedish maritime identity and separate Småland provincial identity ('Smålandsanda'), both dependent on Sweden; no separatism

autarky.rationale: Strong port/road logistics and a diversified industrial base (auto, textile, forestry) support most dimensions evenly; food security benefits from Småland's farmland and forestry economy.

rationales.water: Gota Alv and West Swedish lake network are ample.
rationales.food: Smaland's farmland and forestry economy give a solid regional food score.
rationales.energy: Grid- and hydro-supplied; diversified but not a major domestic generation surplus.

pole.note: Gothenburg dominates West Sweden; Smaland towns (Jonkoping, Vaxjo, Kalmar) are real but secondary.

parliament.name: n/a

regions.name: Malmö / Skåne
regions.identity_basis: Sweden's southernmost province, formerly Danish, with a distinct Scanian (skånsk) dialect and cross-Sound identity oriented toward Copenhagen via the Øresund Bridge.

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Malmö metro ~740,000; Öresund-region hub tightly linked to Copenhagen
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: Medicon Valley life-sciences cluster (with Lund University), Sweden's most productive farmland, Karlskrona naval shipyards
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: distinct Scanian dialect and historical (formerly Danish) identity within Sweden; no separatism despite cross-border Øresund orientation

regions.nuts1_disagreement: NUTS-1 SE2 groups Skåne/Blekinge with Västsverige and Småland-med-öarna; split out as its own mandated Malmö/Skåne node.

rationales.food: Sweden's most productive agricultural region ('breadbasket'); a genuine surplus.

regions.name: Gotland
regions.identity_basis: Sweden's largest Baltic island, with a Gutnish dialect and Hanseatic-era heritage distinct from both mainland Småland and Åland; mandated as its own separate island unit.

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Visby ~24,000; UNESCO World Heritage Hanseatic old town, seat of Region Gotland
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: tourism, agriculture and livestock, limestone quarrying/cement production, fishing
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: distinct Gutnish (gutamål) dialect and island identity, administratively part of Sweden with no separatism; explicitly distinguished from Åland per mandate

regions.nuts1_disagreement: NUTS-2 SE21 (Småland med öarna) bundles Gotland with mainland Jönköping/Kronoberg/Kalmar counties; separated here per the mandated Gotland≠Åland, Gotland-as-its-own-island-unit rule (mainland Småland is folded into the Gothenburg/West Sweden node instead).

autarky.rationale: An isolated Baltic island with decent farmland and limestone resources but limited energy and transport self-sufficiency, dependent on ferry links and mainland grid connections.

rationales.water: A small Baltic island with modest freshwater reserves relative to its limestone geology.

parliament.note: Sweden is a unitary state; regional council only, not a parliament.

regions.name: Upper Norrland
regions.identity_basis: Sweden's Arctic/sub-Arctic north (Vaesterbotten + Norrbotten, NUTS-2 SE33), split out from the former se-norrland record per the draft_v0.1.2 Sapmi-line mandate: this half sits within the Sami homeland (Sapmi) overlay zone shared with Finnish Lapland and North Norway, distinct from Lower Norrland's more temperate, Svealand-adjacent identity.
regions.population_note: Statistics Sweden (SCB) 2023 estimate, Oevre Norrland (NUTS-2 SE33: Vaesterbotten + Norrbotten counties); split from the former se-norrland total (1,757,000) using the two counties' own populations.

conflict_flags.description: Sapmi, the Indigenous Sami homeland, spans northern Finland, Sweden and Norway and is not congruent with any national or NUTS boundary. This is the Swedish-side reference to the same cross-border cultural area already flagged canonically as 'sapmi-cross-border' on fi-lapland-sapmi (given a distinct id here per the project's global conflict_flag-id-uniqueness rule); it flags the overlay without redrawing national region boundaries.

regions.nuts1_disagreement: NUTS-1 SE3 (Norra Sverige) previously grouped this territory with SE31/SE32 as one se-norrland record; split in draft_v0.1.2 at the Sapmi line, mirroring the FI/NO pattern of giving the Sami-homeland north its own cultural unit distinct from the more temperate south.

pole.note: Umeaa (university/cultural hub) and Lulea (steel/tech, Norrbotten's largest city) form a genuine two-pole structure.

parliament.name: Sametinget (Sami Parliament of Sweden)
parliament.note: Sweden is a unitary state with regional councils only, but the Sami Parliament of Sweden has real cultural-autonomy competence over Sami affairs within this Sapmi-zone region -- a genuine partial exception worth the audit's attention.

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Umeaa (~130,000) is the largest city and university/cultural hub; Lulea is Norrbotten's largest city and a steel/tech center
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: iron-ore mining (Kiruna), green-steel and battery investment (Skelleftea/Boden), hydropower, reindeer husbandry
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: distinct Sami/Arctic-Swedish identity within Sweden's Sapmi zone; dependent on, not seeking independence from, Sweden

autarky.rationale: Majority of Sweden's hydropower and abundant fresh water; vast distances and low density limit transportation and healthcare access; food production is modest given the short growing season.

rationales.water: Hosts the majority of Sweden's hydropower reservoirs and abundant fresh water.
rationales.food: Short growing season and sparse arable land keep food production modest.
rationales.energy: Majority of Sweden's hydropower capacity makes this region strongly energy-positive.

regions.name: Lower Norrland
regions.identity_basis: Sweden's more temperate northern-to-central belt (Vaernland, Dalarna, Gaevleborg NUTS-2 SE31 + Vaesternorrland/Jaemtland NUTS-2 SE32), split out from the former se-norrland record per the draft_v0.1.2 Sapmi-line mandate: this half sits south of the Sami-homeland overlay zone and is culturally closer to Svealand, though it retains genuine Norrland regionalist sentiment ('Norrlandsfraagan').
regions.population_note: Statistics Sweden (SCB) 2023 estimate, sum of Norra Mellansverige (NUTS-2 SE31: Vaernland, Dalarna, Gaevleborg) and Mellersta Norrland (NUTS-2 SE32: Vaesternorrland, Jaemtland); the other half of the former se-norrland total (1,757,000).
regions.nuts1_disagreement: NUTS-1 SE3 previously grouped this territory with SE33 as one se-norrland record; split in draft_v0.1.2 at the Sapmi line. SE31 (Vaernland/Dalarna/Gaevleborg, 'Norra Mellansverige') is included here rather than left as a coverage gap, since it borders SE32 directly and no other zone-4 record claims it; this keeps the two split halves summing exactly to the former se-norrland total.

pole.note: No single dominant metropolis; Sundsvall (coastal industrial hub) is the largest, with Oestersund/Karlstad/Falun as comparable secondary poles, mirroring the former se-norrland record's own polycentric-north honesty note.

parliament.note: Sweden is a unitary state; regional councils only, not a parliament.

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Sundsvall (~100,000) is the largest single city; Oestersund, Karlstad and Falun are comparably sized secondary poles rather than clear satellites
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: forestry and pulp, hydropower, steel (Sandviken/Borlaenge), Aare/Siljan tourism
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: genuine Norrland regionalist sentiment ('Norrlandsfraagan') within Sweden, distinct from but adjoining the Sami-homeland Upper Norrland to its north; no separatism

autarky.rationale: Extensive hydropower and forestry-linked biomass keep energy strong; food production is moderate given the short growing season further north but Vaernland/Gaevleborg farmland helps; a dispersed polycentric settlement pattern limits transportation and specialist healthcare access.

rationales.water: Extensive lake district (Siljan, Storsjoen) and river network give strong per-capita supply.
rationales.food: Vaernland/Gaevleborg farmland is more productive than the Arctic north, giving a moderate food score.
rationales.energy: Hydropower (Indalsaelven) and forestry biomass keep this region energy-strong.

inclusion_test.diversified_industry: pharmaceuticals/life sciences, global shipping, finance, EU/government administration, agriculture on rural Zealand
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: clear Copenhagen-metropolitan identity within Denmark, including Bornholm's distinct Baltic-island character; no separatism

rationales.food: Rural Zealand farmland supports solid food security despite the dense capital population.
rationales.energy: Draws on Denmark's wind fleet, but capital demand keeps this below the Jutland wind heartland.

regions.name: Jutland & Funen

regions.name: Oslo & Eastern/Southern Norway
regions.identity_basis: Norway's capital and its densely populated eastern/southern commuter and agricultural hinterland (Østfold, Akershus, Innlandet, Buskerud, Vestfold, Telemark, Agder); the country's political and financial core, mandated as distinct from the western/northern fjord-culture nodes.

inclusion_test.urban_hub: Oslo metro ~1.1M; national capital, Oslo Stock Exchange, government seat
inclusion_test.diversified_industry: finance and shipping services, ICT, Østfold/Akershus grain agriculture, Telemark/Agder process industry (aluminium, petrochemicals)

Eastern/southern Norway (NO08 Oslo og Viken, NO09 Agder og Sør-Østlandet, NO02 Innlandet) is grouped under Oslo as its dominant, commuter-linked metropolitan hinterland rather than given a separate un-mandated node. Note: the raw GISCO NUTS_RG_20M_2024 geometry file still ships pre-2024-restructuring NUTS2 groupings (NO02/NO06/NO07/NO08/NO09) rather than the newer SR2024 NO0C/NO0D/NO0E scheme listed in data/nuts_index.json; codes here were adjusted to match the actual geometry, per the build pipeline's resolution requirement.

autarky.rationale: Extensive hydropower and glacial/mountain water give near-total energy and water self-sufficiency; food security is moderate given limited arable land relative to population, offset by Østfold/Akershus grain farming.

rationales.water: Extensive hydropower and glacial/mountain water give near-total self-sufficiency.
rationales.food: Moderate given limited arable land relative to population, offset by Ostfold/Akershus grain farming.

regions.name: Stavanger-Bergen

inclusion_test.diversified_industry: North Sea oil/gas headquarters (Equinor), subsea engineering, salmon aquaculture, fjord tourism
inclusion_test.dependent_identity: distinct Vestlandet fjord-culture and nynorsk-language identity within Norway; no separatism

rationales.energy: Strong hydropower keeps this region energy-strong.

regions.name: Ålesund / Northwest Norway
regions.identity_basis: Norway's northwestern fjord and fishing coast, with a distinctive Art Nouveau port city (Ålesund) and a strong maritime-fishing culture distinct from both Bergen/Stavanger to the south and Trøndelag to the north; mandated as its own node.

inclusion_test.diversified_industry: seafood export/processing, maritime equipment and shipbuilding supply, furniture manufacturing

rationales.energy: Hydropower keeps this region energy-strong despite fragmented fjord/island geography limiting transport.
