Iparralde (French Basque Country): no separate Iparralde region is authored here. Aquitaine/Bordeaux retains its full historic-Aquitaine codes including FRI15 (Pyrénées-Atlantiques). German-Netherlands border micro-culture: flagged as a conflict_flags layer on the Zuid-Nederland (South-NL) region, covering all three Limburg NUTS-3 units (NL421/NL422/NL423), reflecting the Limburgish dialect continuum across the Dutch-German border.

Corsica is authored as its own region (NUTS-1 FRM) with a mandated identity/autonomy conflict_flags entry; the conflict is about internal autonomy status, not cross-border unification, hence a conflict_flag rather than a variant set.

Parliament rule note (zone2): all French records carry parliament.has_own true for their conseils régionaux with the explicit caveat 'administrative region council, not a legislative parliament' — France is a unitary state and no French région legislates, so the parliament rule does NOT force further FR splits. Where a unit spans two former administrative régions (e.g. fr-pays-de-la-loire incl. Centre-Val de Loire) the note lists both councils. Belgian Flanders/Wallonia/Brussels have genuine legislative parliaments (has_own true). Dutch provinces have Provinciale Staten (provincial councils, not parliaments) — has_own false with note. Luxembourg's Chambre des Députés is a sovereign national parliament.
Overseas French territories (NUTS-1 FRY) remain out of scope per Global Constraints.

Population figures for merged/split regions are sums of constituent NUTS-2/3 populations from Eurostat/INSEE/CBS/Statbel 2022-2023 regional statistics; splits (Auvergne, Burgundy-Franche-Comté, Champagne, NL units) were recomputed from the same sources and flagged via population_note.

PT COVERAGE — SCOPE EXPANDED BEYOND THE NAMED 'ALENTEJO' ITEM: the content brief named only Alentejo as a PT coverage task, but the v1 zone notes (superseded below) already documented THREE uncovered mainland Portuguese NUTS-2 units — Alentejo (PT1C), Oeste e Vale do Tejo (PT1D), and Centro (PT19) — and the blocking >=0.97 coverage test cannot pass while Centro (a large, populous unit including Coimbra/Aveiro/Viseu/Leiria) remains empty basemap. Resolution: (1) pt-alentejo authored as its OWN unit rather than an extension of Lisbon southward — identity-true reasoning: Alentejo's rural-agrarian/cork-wine/cante-alentejano identity is genuinely distinct from capital-region Lisbon, so 'Lisbon covers the entire south' would misrepresent rather than honestly reflect a weak-but-real identity (same standard as Calabria/Algarve in v1); the 'Lisbon absorbs the south' idea is instead honored at the REPRESENTATION (groupings) layer, where pt-alentejo is grouped with pt-lisbon. GROUPINGS authored in data/groupings/zone3.json: 23 representation-layer groupings partition all 45 default_visible zone3 cultural units (the two flagship capital-regions Madrid and Lazio/Rome plus Catalonia are each kept as their own singleton grouping to preserve the site's flagship framing and Rome/Madrid capital-region parallel; the composites es-greater-castile, es-madrid-extended, and basque-unified are default_visible:false and correctly excluded from the grouping partition). Where a real Eurostat NUTS-1 partition exists (Spain's Noroeste/Noreste/Centro/Este/Sur classification; Italy's Nord-Est/Centro/Sud/Isole classification), it is used as the grouping's sourced basis rather than an ad hoc judgment call, with explicit deviations flagged (Catalonia pulled out of NUTS-1 Este; Lazio out of NUTS-1 Centro; Lombardy kept within Nord-Ovest rather than pulled out; Sicily/Sardinia/Campania/Puglia kept standalone rather than merged into NUTS-1 Isole/Sud, given each region's own mandated-distinct special-statute or population-scale standing). TENSION FLAG: this yields 23 groupings for zone3 alone, above the brief's '~aim 10-14' guidance. Zone3 is the dataset's largest single zone (45 of the broader dataset's default-visible units); forcing further consolidation into fewer, larger groupings was avoided where it would have produced geographically/culturally incoherent blobs (e.g. merging Basque Country into a generic 'Atlantic Spain' bucket, or Sicily into an undifferentiated 'Isole' seat alongside Sardinia). Consistent with this project's established precedent of letting the total region count emerge from criteria rather than truncating to hit a target (see the original 36-vs-24-30 flag above), the groupings count is left to emerge here too, with the deviation stated explicitly for the methodology page and for reconciliation against the dataset-wide 40-70 representation-layer target once all zones' groupings fragments are combined.

Zone 3 covers Iberia + Italy (ES, PT, IT). Region count came to 36 records (34 distinct territorial regions plus the congruent/noncongruent Basque pair) in v1, above the ~24-30 rough estimate given for this zone but consistent with the global constraint's instruction to let the count emerge from the inclusion test rather than truncate: Italy alone has 19 records because its 20 traditional administrative regions (here 19 after the Abruzzo-Molise merge) are each genuinely distinct cultural-administrative units with recognized identities, and Spain contributes 12 because its autonomous-community structure is similarly fine-grained. This zone's contribution to the dataset's overall 40-70 (up to 90-110) tension is flagged here for the methodology page.

Basque Country is authored as both a congruent record (es-basque: Euskadi ES21 + Navarre ES22, urban core Bilbao as mandated) and a noncongruent unified record (basque-unified: ES21+ES22+FRI15, spanning ES+FR). The unified record's only available French-side NUTS unit, FRI15 (Pyrénées-Atlantiques), also covers Béarn — a distinct, non-Basque (Occitan/Gascon) territory east of Iparralde proper — so the unified boundary overstates the true Basque-cultural extent on the French side. This is recorded as a conflict_flag on basque-unified rather than silently corrected, since no finer (arrondissement-level) NUTS geometry is available in the index.

South Tyrol is authored ONLY as the congruent record (it-south-tyrol, NUTS-2 ITH1/Provincia Autonoma di Bolzano). The noncongruent unified 'tyrol-unified' record (joining Austrian Tirol) is authored in zone1.json per the cross-zone coordination plan.

Iceland (IS) is not on the Global Constraints single-unit-exception list, yet is modeled here as one region. Reasoning: ~64% of the population lives in the Reykjavík capital area, and no second city (Akureyri, ~19,000) approaches a comparable diversified industrial base or cultural-hub status; Iceland is also linguistically and culturally homogeneous with no internal regionalist movement. It is therefore treated as a de-facto single unit while explicitly NOT added to the formal exception list, per the zone brief's instruction to state the reasoning rather than silently reclassify it.

Norrland (northern Sweden) was assessed against the three-part inclusion test and included as its own region despite lacking one dominant metropolis (Umeå, Sundsvall and Luleå are comparably sized secondary poles). It passes on the strength of a genuine regionalist identity ('Norrlandsfrågan'), a highly diversified industrial base (hydropower, forestry, mining), and its sheer land area (~half of Sweden). This is flagged as a softer pass than the zone's other, single-metro-anchored regions.

Mainland Småland (Jönköping, Kronoberg, Kalmar counties) has no dedicated mandate in the zone brief and was folded into the Gothenburg/West Sweden region rather than left as a coverage gap, since NUTS2024 groups it at NUTS-2 (SE21) with Gotland — which must be split out per the Gotland-as-separate-island mandate — leaving mainland Småland without a natural standalone NUTS grouping distinct from West Sweden's economic orbit.

Two areas were deliberately left OUT of the zone-4 region set as coverage gaps rather than force-fitted into a neighboring identity: (1) Finland's eastern lakeland provinces (Etelä-Savo/Pohjois-Savo/Pohjois-Karjala, i.e. the Kuopio/Joensuu/Mikkeli 'Savo-Karelia' area) — genuinely distinct in dialect and identity from both the Oulu and Helsinki nodes, but not separately mandated, so excluded pending a dedicated inclusion-test pass in a future revision; (2) Svalbard and Jan Mayen (NO0B) — near-uninhabited Norwegian Arctic territories that fail the inclusion test outright (no functioning urban cultural hub, no diversified industrial base beyond research/tourism outposts).

The Sápmi Indigenous homeland spans northern Finland, Sweden and Norway and is not congruent with any national or NUTS boundary. Rather than redraw national region boundaries, it is represented as a conflict_flag overlay on the Finnish Lapland/Sápmi region (fi-lapland-sapmi), with zone_nuts_codes spanning FI1D7 (Lappi), SE331/SE332 (Västerbotten/Norrbotten) and NO071/NO072/NO073 (Nordland/Troms/Finnmark) — deliberately overlapping the base nuts_codes of the Norrland and Tromsø/North regions, since conflict flags are overlays, not exclusive territorial claims.

Count tension: applying every fixed zone-4 mandate at face value (5 distinct Finnish nodes + Åland; 3 distinct Swedish nodes + Gotland + assessed Norrland; 2 Danish nodes; 5 distinct Norwegian fjord-culture nodes; Iceland; 3 Baltic single units; Greenland + Faroe Islands) yields 24 regions, above the zone brief's 'roughly 18-22' estimate. Per the Global Constraints instruction to flag rather than silently truncate such tension, this is noted explicitly here instead of merging any of the individually mandated, identity-distinct nodes to hit the lower estimate.

Norway's SR2024 county geometry reflects the 2024 restructuring following the 2020-2024 Viken/Troms-og-Finnmark mergers being reversed back into Østfold, Akershus, Buskerud, Troms and Finnmark as separate counties; the no-oslo-eastern-southern-norway region's population figure sums these post-2024 county boundaries rather than the short-lived 2020-2023 merged-county structure.

Svalbard and Jan Mayen (Norwegian Arctic territories, NUTS code NO0B) are deliberately excluded from this zone's region set: near-uninhabited, no functioning urban cultural hub, no diversified industrial base beyond research/tourism outposts, and outside this dataset's practical-regions scope (methodology note, not a silent coverage gap).

NUTS-vintage policy: authored nuts_codes in this file follow the GISCO 2024 geometry vintage (NUTS_RG_20M_2024_4326.geojson) wherever the NUTS 2027 recoding (reflected in the xlsx used for data/nuts_index.json) has since renumbered a country's units -- e.g. Norway's 2024 county-geometry codes (NO02/06/07/08/09/0A1/0A2/0A3) rather than the 2027-sheet's NO0C/D/E; the same policy applies to Belgium's 2024-vintage BE21/23 (vs. the 2027 recoding's BE26/27) and Bulgaria's BG3/BG4-vs-BG5x recoding elsewhere in this dataset. This keeps every authored code resolvable against the committed geometry file rather than a future labeling vintage the pipeline cannot yet render.

draft_v0.1.2 schema v2 migration: variant_group/variant_role removed; default_visible added (all zone4 units remain default_visible true -- no variant sets are mandated for the Nordics/Baltics in this content wave, so data/variant_sets/zone4.json is an empty array). pole (with mandated central_coord/secondary_coord per Amendment A1.4), parliament, and lang_family added to every unit. autarky.rationales added for water/food/energy on every unit per Amendment A1.6 (other four dimensions left for a future beta pass).

A1.10 Norrland split (draft_v0.1.2, new): se-norrland is split at the Sami-homeland (Sapmi) line, mirroring the Finnish/Norwegian pattern of giving the Sapmi-zone north its own unit. se-norrland-upper (SE33: Vaesterbotten+Norrbotten, Umeaa/Lulea) sits within the same Sapmi conflict_flag overlay already shared with fi-lapland-sapmi and no-tromso-north-norway. se-norrland-lower (SE31+SE32: Vaernland/Dalarna/Gaevleborg + Vaesternorrland/Jaemtland, Sundsvall/Oestersund) absorbs SE31 ('Norra Mellansverige') for coverage continuity, since the plan's own wording named only SE32 explicitly ('Sundsvall/Oestersund') -- SE31 is not separately mandated a home and would otherwise become a silent coverage gap; flagged here as an editorial inclusion rather than a literal mandate.

Innlandet / no-alesund-northwest reallocation -- UNSATISFIABLE AT LITERAL GRANULARITY (draft_v0.1.2 content-wave finding, flagged not silently resolved): the plan asks for a 'reasoned reallocation' giving Aalesund/Northwest Norway 'more of Innlandet' via 'adjust NUTS-3 code assignment'. Verified against the committed 2024 GISCO geometry (pipeline/raw/NUTS_RG_20M_2024_4326.geojson): Innlandet ships as a single undivided NUTS-3-equivalent feature (NO020) under NO02, with no finer sub-code available to split between the historically west-facing Gudbrandsdalen/Rauma-corridor communities (Dombaas-Aandalsnes, genuinely oriented toward Aalesund via the Rauma railway/E136) and the east-facing Hedmark/central-Gudbrandsdalen communities (oriented toward Oslo via the Mjosa/E6 corridor). Moving the entire NO02 code to no-alesund-northwest would misassign Hedmark, which is clearly Oslo-facing; moving nothing would ignore the mandate outright. Resolution taken: the NUTS code stays with no-oslo-eastern-southern-norway (unchanged), and no-alesund-northwest instead carries a documented `reach` entry into the Gudbrandsdalen/Rauma corridor (functional/cultural reach, not a territorial code reassignment). This item could not be honored literally without either a finer geometry source or an honest all-or-nothing code move that would misrepresent Hedmark; flagged for the controller/audit per the project's standing convention of stating such tensions rather than silently truncating or forcing an incorrect reallocation.

Zone 5 (UK + Ireland) uses nuts_source NUTS2021 for all UK-side codes, since the UK's post-Brexit exit from Eurostat's 2024 NUTS release means UK boundaries only resolve against the GISCO NUTS_RG_20M_2021_4326.geojson file; Ireland-side codes use NUTS2024 except where a single record (ireland-unified) must combine IE and UK codes under one nuts_source, in which case NUTS2021 is used because the 2021 GISCO file happens to still carry both countries' geometries.

The London commuter-belt region (~18.3M) is an order of magnitude larger by population than most other regions in this zone (570k-5.95M) and in the dataset generally. This mirrors real economic geography (London's functional region genuinely dominates UK demography) but creates a scale asymmetry flagged here for the methodology page's discussion of the 40-70 vs 90-110 region-count tension: a finer-grained alternative would split it further into a Thames Valley/Berks-Bucks-Oxon region, a Kent region, and a Bedfordshire-Hertfordshire-Essex region, at the cost of adding three more small, thin-identity regions to an already London-dominated zone.

Sussex and the London-commuter-belt region both draw on NUTS-2 code UKJ2 ('Surrey, East and West Sussex'), which bundles two functionally distinct areas (commuter-belt Surrey and coastal/identity-distinct Sussex) below the level the fixed decisions mandate splitting them at. This required descending to NUTS-3 for that single NUTS-2 unit (Surrey's UKJ25/UKJ26 to the commuter belt, Sussex's UKJ21/UKJ22/UKJ27/UKJ28 to Sussex) while every other UK region in this zone stays at NUTS-1 or NUTS-2 granularity -- an explicit exception to the 'coarsest exact-cover' preference, justified by the mandated Sussex/London-commuter split.

Cornwall is kept distinct from the Exeter-Plymouth/West Country region despite a small, weakly urbanised population and a comparatively weak single-city inclusion-test score, on the strength of the Cornish people's 2014 UK-government recognition as a national minority under the Council of Europe Framework Convention -- a stronger and more specific evidentiary basis than the generic historic-county identities used to justify Wessex or the West Country.

Liverpool/Merseyside is kept distinct from Manchester/North West despite immediate geographic adjacency and a shared NUTS-1 region (UKD), on the strength of a genuinely distinct Scouse dialect/identity, a separate 19th-century transatlantic-port and Irish-diaspora heritage, and a separate Liverpool City Region devolution settlement with its own directly elected mayor.

East Anglia/Cambridge is kept distinct from the London commuter belt: although East Anglia sits within the same NUTS-1 East of England region (UKH) as Bedfordshire/Hertfordshire/Essex, the latter three counties are reassigned to the London commuter-belt region as functionally London-oriented, while Cambridgeshire/Peterborough/Norfolk/Suffolk retain a coherent flatland-agricultural identity and a globally significant 'Silicon Fen' knowledge-economy cluster independent of London's gravity.

Scotland is split into a Central Belt region (Glasgow-Edinburgh-Southern Uplands, NUTS-2 UKM7/UKM8/UKM9) and a Highlands and Islands region (NUTS-2 UKM5/UKM6), assessed and adopted per the mandate. The Highlands region includes Aberdeen and Aberdeenshire (NUTS-2 UKM5, 'North Eastern Scotland') for population parsimony, even though Aberdeen's oil-and-gas urban economy is culturally North East Lowland rather than Gaelic Highland; a three-way Central Belt / North East (Aberdeen) / Highlands-Islands split would be more identity-accurate but was not adopted here to avoid a third, thinly populated Scottish region, and is flagged for methodology discussion alongside the analogous Hungary subdivision question in Zone 6.

East Midlands (NUTS-1 UKF: Derbyshire/Nottinghamshire, Leicestershire/Rutland/Northamptonshire, Lincolnshire) was originally assessed and excluded from this zone's region list as a coverage gap (~4.9M people, the arithmetic difference between the ONS UK total and the sum of this file's other UK regions), on the grounds that Nottingham, Leicester and Derby form a genuinely polycentric conurbation with no single dominant city, unlike Birmingham, Manchester, Leeds or Newcastle. Task 4 dataset QA revisited this decision and added uk-east-midlands (NUTS2021 UKF) to close the gap, with the polycentric fit noted honestly in its inclusion_test rather than silently smoothed over -- see that record for the full reasoning.

Ireland variant handling (schema v2): uk-northern-ireland, ie-dublin, ie-cork and ie-galway are the default_visible cultural units; ireland-unified (default_visible false) appears only via the 'ireland' variant set in data/variant_sets/zone58.json. Per controller amendment A1, Northern Ireland stays visible as a DISTINCT unit in every view of the set - including the unified view, where it renders on top of the all-island polygon so the contested border remains legible rather than being dissolved away.

All UK autarky and population figures in this file are approximate: ONS/NISRA/CSO publish detailed figures at local-authority and NUTS-3 level, but this file aggregates to the custom region boundaries defined above, which do not correspond 1:1 to any single published statistical release. Figures should be treated as directionally reliable estimates for methodology and comparative purposes, not as official regional statistics.

Schema v2 migration (draft-v0.1.2): variant_group/variant_role removed; default_visible, special_status, pole (with central_coord/secondary_coord per amendment A1), reach, parliament, lang_family and autarky.rationales (water/food/energy) added to every record. Pole assignments are best-effort characterisations: capital-dominated regions are monopoles; Southampton-Portsmouth, Exeter-Plymouth, Cambridge-Norwich, Edinburgh-Glasgow, Aberdeen-Inverness and Preston-Lancaster are dipoles; Yorkshire and the East Midlands are polycentric.

Lancashire split (draft-v0.1.2 mandate): the former 'Greater Manchester and the North West' region is divided into uk-manchester (Greater Manchester, UKD3) and uk-lancashire (Lancashire + Cumbria, UKD4 + UKD1) with the mandated Preston+Lancaster dual pole. Cumbria goes with Lancashire, not Manchester: once Lancashire is split out, UKD1 would be non-contiguous with UKD3, and south Cumbria's historic ('Lancashire over the Sands') and functional (Lancaster gateway) orientation is Lancastrian.

Dublin-Cavan reach (draft-v0.1.2 mandate): the user mandate places Cavan in Dublin's orbit. Cavan lies in NUTS-3 IE041 ('Border') together with Donegal, Sligo, Leitrim and Monaghan; no finer geometry exists in the pipeline, so moving IE041 wholesale to ie-dublin would absurdly attach Donegal to the capital region. The boundary therefore stays at the IE06/IE04 line and Dublin's pull on Cavan is recorded as a reach entry on ie-dublin - an honest data-granularity limitation, not a rejection of the mandate.

Crown Dependencies (coverage sweep): Guernsey (gg-guernsey), Jersey (je-jersey) and the Isle of Man (im-isle-of-man) are added as units with CNTR geometry (GISCO CNTR_RG_20M_2024 carries CNTR_ID GG/JE/IM - no geoBoundaries fallback needed, unlike Ukraine). Each keeps its own parliament (States of Guernsey, States Assembly of Jersey, Tynwald), satisfying the parliament rule, and carries special_status 'Crown Dependency' (dashed stroke): they are self-governing Crown possessions, not part of the UK. Guernsey and Jersey are modelled as separate units rather than one 'Channel Islands' unit precisely because each Bailiwick has its own legislature.

lang_family tags are approximate single-value identity tags for the linguistic perspective lens: 'celtic' for Wales, Cornwall, the Highlands, the Irish units and the Isle of Man (Manx) reflects identity-defining heritage languages rather than majority speech (English dominates everywhere); Guernsey and Jersey are tagged 'romance' for their Norman langue-d'oil heritage; Northern Ireland is tagged 'germanic' (English/Ulster-Scots majority speech) while its Irish-community identity is covered by the variant set rather than the language tag.

HUNGARY PUSH-BACK VERDICT (mandated challenge, v0.1.0, SUPERSEDED for v0.1.2): the brief originally proposed a four-way Hungarian subdivision — Budapest / Győr-Western Transdanubia / Pécs-Southern Transdanubia / Szombathely-Balaton — which v0.1.0 rejected down to 2 regions (hu-budapest, hu-videk) for the reasons preserved below. draft_v0.1.2's content brief explicitly OVERRIDES that v0.1.0 verdict: the user re-mandated exactly 4 Hungarian units (Budapest; West/Szombathely; Lake Balaton; East/Debrecen), acknowledging the v0.1.0 identity critique but choosing finer administrative units anyway, with the GROUPINGS layer (data/groupings/zone67.json) re-collapsing them for representation (grp-hu-budapest, grp-hu-videk) — the two-layer cultural-atom/representation-group model added in v0.1.2 is precisely what makes this supersession clean: Hungary's Budapest-centralized political-cultural identity is preserved at the grouping layer even though the cultural-unit layer now has 4 finer atoms. All 20 HU NUTS-3 codes are covered exactly once across hu-budapest/hu-west/hu-balaton/hu-east-debrecen (verified programmatically). Two coverage-driven extensions beyond the user's literal 4-name list are stated plainly in the affected records rather than silently absorbed: (a) Fejér and Komárom-Esztergom (the Közép-Dunántúl remainder once Veszprém moves to Balaton) join hu-budapest as its western commuter-industrial periphery; (b) Baranya and Tolna (the Dél-Dunántúl remainder once Somogy moves to Balaton) join hu-balaton, producing the honest tension that hu-balaton's largest city (Pécs) sits ~150km from the lake itself. v0.1.0's original push-back evidence (Assembly of European Regions 2021; regscience.hu) is retained below as background — it remains true that Hungary's abolished NUTS-2 planning regions never acquired organic identity; the user's re-mandate is understood as choosing administrative-geographic fineness for map purposes over strict identity-purity, which the schema v2 two-layer model now accommodates without contradiction. [v0.1.0 text retained:] Three WebSearch-verified findings: (1) Hungary's NUTS-2 regions were imposed top-down under EU pressure in 1999 and never acquired an organic regional identity — 'the failure of regional reforms can be explained not just by the lack of regional identity, but rather by the unwillingness of the central political elite to decentralize ... top-down regionalisation ... failed to create a regional identity' (Assembly of European Regions, 2021; regscience.hu). (2) Where genuine sub-national identity DOES surface in Hungary, it operates at the county (megye) level. (3) Hungarian dialectology (Transdanubian vs. Alföld) rides on no organized regionalist movement.

SLOVAKIA A1.8 SUPERSEDES v0.1.0's Bratislava-west/Košice-east 2-way split composition: the two units are RETAINED (still exactly 2) but Eastern Slovakia is renamed sk-east and re-modeled as a Košice-Prešov DIPOLE (SK041+SK042) rather than a Košice-dominant single pole, foregrounding the Rusyn/Ukrainian minority concentrated in Prešov kraj as co-equal identity basis alongside Košice's steel/industrial economy. sk-bratislava-west is unchanged in composition (SK01+SK02+SK03) with its Central-Slovakia/SNP-heritage reasoning restated per A1.8's request.

CROATIA A1.9 SUPERSEDES v0.1.0's 3-way split (Zagreb-Continental / Dalmatia / Istria-Rijeka merged): Rijeka/Kvarner is carved out as its OWN 4th unit (hr-rijeka, HR031), isolating its distinct Fiuman/Habsburg-port-city civic heritage from Istria's bilingual Croatian-Italian regionalist identity (hr-istria, HR036 alone). hr-zagreb-continental and hr-dalmatia are unchanged in composition; Ličko-senjska (Lika) stays attached to hr-dalmatia per v1 rather than moving to hr-rijeka despite arguably closer geographic/hinterland ties to Rijeka — flagged as a candidate future reassignment rather than silently resolved.

SILESIA CROSS-BORDER VARIANT SET (A1.13): Upper Silesia (pl-silesia, Katowice) and Czech Silesia (cz-czech-silesia, Ostrava) are unchanged as separate congruent-with-current-states records (the "current" view of the new "silesia" variant set in data/variant_sets/zone67.json), but a new hidden noncongruent record silesia-unified (default_visible false, PL22+PL52+CZ08) is added for the "connected" and "overlap" views, following the same pattern as tyrol-unified in zone1. Bielsko-Biała is explicitly noted as a borderland inclusion within pl-silesia (administratively Śląskie voivodeship, culturally transitional toward Lesser Poland/Galicia) per A1.13's instruction.

SLOVENIA A1.5 SUPERSEDES ITS OWN EARLIER AMENDMENT: an East/West (Maribor-Štajerska vs. Ljubljana-and-west) variant set was drafted for the original C4 dispatch (SI03 Vzhodna Slovenija vs. SI04 Zahodna Slovenija, a clean pre-existing NUTS-2 boundary), then explicitly REJECTED by the user before this file was finalized ('small enough as it is') — DROPPED entirely per A1.5, not even retained as a hidden fragment. si-slovenia stays the single-unit exception it always was, now with schema v2 fields added.

SILESIAN IDENTITY (Poland, pl-silesia conflict_flag): the 2021 Polish census recorded 596,224 self-declarations of Silesian nationality (down from 846,700 in 2011), a decline Polish sociologists (e.g. Prof. Małgorzata Myśliwiec, University of Silesia) partly attribute to the harder-to-navigate online census form rather than a real decline in Silesian self-identification. Silesian nationality remains formally unrecognized by the Polish state.

MORAVIAN IDENTITY (Czechia, cz-moravia): the 2021 Czech census recorded 359,621 Moravian-nationality declarations (5.0% of respondents, down from 522,474 in 2011), with dual Czech-Moravian declarations rising ~80% to 179,721. Concentration reaches 21.6% in Jihomoravský (Brno region), 15.0% in Zlínský and 12.4% in Olomoucký.

POLAND REGION COUNT (8 visible regions covering all 16 voivodeships, no gaps/overlaps, unchanged from v0.1.0): Opolskie attaches to Katowice/Silesia rather than Wrocław/Lower Silesia on shared Upper-Silesian dialect/German-minority grounds; Szczecin/Zachodniopomorskie and Lubuskie fold into Poznań/Wielkopolska matching NUTS-1 PL4; Podkarpackie/Lubelskie/Podlaskie/Świętokrzyskie merge into one Eastern Poland bloc matching the EU's own 'Polska Wschodnia' category. v0.1.2 additionally authors a hidden 3-way SPLIT variant view of pl-pomerania (pl-kashubia-core/pl-kuyavia/pl-warmia-masuria, all default_visible false) per the mandated "pomerania" variant set, demonstrating the Kashubia(strong)/Kuyavia(weak)/Warmia-Masuria(weakest) fit-strength gradient the broad default view otherwise papers over.

SCHEMA v2 MIGRATION NOTE: this file has no v1 variant_group/variant_role members (the old tyrol-style congruent/noncongruent pairing was never used in zone6), so every pre-existing region defaults to default_visible: true with no ambiguity. pole/parliament/reach/lang_family/special_status/autarky.rationales are new v2 additions per the draft_v0.1.2 plan; parliament.has_own is marked true-with-note for PL/CZ/SK (real elected regional assemblies — sejmiki/zastupitelstva/samosprávne kraje — exist but this cultural unit's multi-voivodeship/kraj composition means several co-exist per unit, flagged for the CA parliament_exceptions audit) and false for HU/HR/SI-country-level-true (Hungarian megyei and Croatian županije assemblies are deconcentrated-administrative, no legislative function, per the explicit HR audit rule extended consistently to HU).

ZONE 7 SCOPE AND COUNT (v0.1.0, background): this file originally authored 22 regions across RO/BG/GR/CY/MT/RS/BA/ME/MK/AL/XK. draft_v0.1.2 raises this to 26 default-visible regions via three mandated supersessions: RO gains ro-szekely-land (A1.12, +1); GR splits gr-thessaloniki-macedonia into gr-macedonia + gr-thrace (+1); BA's single region becomes 3 entity-level units (+2). Per Global Constraint #4 ('let the count emerge from criteria... flag this tension explicitly, do NOT silently truncate'), no compensating merges were made elsewhere in this zone to hold the count down — see data/groupings/zone67.json for how the representation layer re-consolidates.

SZEKELY LAND (RO, A1.12 mandate): Covasna, Harghita and Mureș counties are carved out of Transylvania as their own visible cultural unit, ro-szekely-land. This is this zone's most contested application of the third inclusion-test criterion (dependent, not seeking independence): a real, organized Székely autonomy movement exists (Szekler National Council), closer to the separatism/autonomy line than any other region in this file, though it stops short of an independence claim and has no current legal standing under Romanian law. The conflict_flags overlay is RETAINED on ro-transylvania per the mandate, even though the territory itself is now a separate visible unit — the overlay marks the historic Hungarian/Saxon minority layer that predates and exceeds the modern county boundaries.

GREECE MACEDONIA/THRACE SPLIT (mandated): the former gr-thessaloniki-macedonia (EL51+EL52+EL53) splits along the EL51 (Thrace) / EL52+EL53 (Macedonia proper) boundary, isolating Western Thrace's Lausanne-Treaty-protected Muslim minority (Turkish, Pomak, Roma) as its own visible unit. IONIAN ISLANDS VERDICT: kept attached to gr-peloponnese-central-greece (renamed 'Peloponnese, Central Greece & Ionian Islands' for clarity) as the 'northern/western mainland' attachment the brief's decision criterion names, on the strength of the islands' geographic adjacency to Epirus/Western Greece (not the Aegean) and ferry/administrative ties to the opposite mainland coast — a borderline call stated explicitly rather than left ambiguous. THESSALONIKI REACH: gr-macedonia carries a reach entry into North Macedonia (Skopje's historic sea-outlet via the Vardar/Axios corridor), stated as an economic-geography fact given the post-2019 Prespa Agreement's naming sensitivity, not a territorial claim.

CYPRUS GEOMETRY VERDICT (checked, not fabricated): the plan asked us to check for a Greek/Turkish Cypriot geometry source within 5 minutes before falling back to a single flagged region. Two checks were made: (1) the committed GISCO NUTS2024 raw geometry file (pipeline/raw/NUTS_RG_20M_2024_4326.geojson) carries only whole-island CY/CY0/CY00/CY000 — verified programmatically, no sub-island feature exists. (2) A live geoBoundaries API check (github.com/wmgeolab/geoBoundaries, CYP ADM1) found exactly 6 administrative units, but these are Cyprus's 6 historic PRE-1974 districts (Nicosia, Limassol, Larnaca, Famagusta, Paphos, Kyrenia) — several of which (notably Nicosia and Famagusta) are themselves bisected by the 1974 Green Line, meaning using them as a north/south proxy would misrepresent the actual de facto division rather than depict it. VERDICT (per the plan's own pre-authorized fallback): kept as ONE region, single_unit_exception unchanged (true), added special_status ('cy-defacto-division', dashed rendering) and a strengthened conflict_flag documenting the limitation explicitly as 'north/south split pending geometry source' — a deliberate, stated limitation rather than a fabricated boundary.

BOSNIA AND HERZEGOVINA SUPERSEDES v0.1.0's single-region-with-flag verdict (SUPERSEDED, not merely refined): the 1995 Dayton entities — Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Republika Srpska, Brčko District — are now three separate cultural units, each carrying its own real constitutional parliament (Parliament of the Federation, National Assembly of Republika Srpska, Brčko District Assembly), satisfying the schema v2 parliament rule directly. IMPORTANT PIPELINE FINDING, obviating the plan's own hedge: the plan anticipated needing a 'BA_ADM1'/geoBoundaries/shapeName-based workaround if the SR2024 sub-codes lacked geometry. They do NOT lack geometry — BA01 (Federacija Bosne i Hercegovine), BA02 (Republika Srpska) and BA03 (Brčko distrikt) all resolve directly against the SAME committed GISCO raw geometry file used for every other region in this dataset (pipeline/raw/NUTS_RG_20M_2024_4326.geojson), verified programmatically before authoring. NO pipeline coordination, workaround, or geoBoundaries fetch is needed for BA — this should simplify, not complicate, Task P's integration. v0.1.0's original 'Dayton partition is not organic regionalism' argument is preserved as background in each entity's conflict_flags/identity_basis rather than deleted, since it remains true as a historical claim even though the parliament rule now overrides it as the operative criterion. The three BA units are re-collapsed into ONE 'Bosnia & Herzegovina' representation grouping in data/groupings/zone67.json, per the explicit two-layer model instruction.

SLOVAKIA/HUNGARY/CROATIA cross-references: see data/regions/zone6.json notes for the A1.8 (Slovakia), Hungary-4-unit-supersession, and A1.9 (Croatia/Rijeka) methodology — those countries are authored in zone6, not here, but interact with this file's groupings (data/groupings/zone67.json spans both zones).

SCHEMA v2 FIELD CONVENTIONS FOR THIS FILE: parliament.has_own is true for RO/BG/GR county-equivalent administrative units per the explicit 'HR/RO/BG counties no' rule extended consistently to Greek perifereies (false for all of them); true for Vojvodina (real constitutional Autonomous Province Assembly) and false for central Serbia (no separate assembly); true for all three BA entities (real Dayton-constitutional legislatures) and re-collapsed at the grouping layer; true for every single-unit-exception sovereign country in this zone (CY/MT/ME/MK/AL/XK — each unit IS the whole state, so 'own parliament' means the national parliament) and false for Székely Land (no current legal parliament exists, despite the active autonomy movement — this is precisely why it does not get a standalone representation grouping the way Vojvodina and the BA entities collectively do).

Kaliningrad Oblast, a Russian exclave of roughly 15,000 km2 and ~1.0 million residents wedged between Poland and Lithuania on the Baltic coast, is geographically inside the mapped space of this dataset but is not included as a region record or geometry: it is non-EU Russian sovereign territory, cut off from mainland Russia by the 1945 territorial reorganisation that renamed the formerly German/Prussian city of Konigsberg (annexed from Germany, its ethnic-German population expelled) as Kaliningrad. It is rendered in the map legend and methodology purely as a text note, per the Global Constraints' instruction to acknowledge it as a geographic exclave note despite falling outside the EU+neighbours+microstates scope of this framework.

Ukraine's 27 SR2024 level-2 units are grouped into twelve regions (draft-v0.1.2): six mandated distinct (Kyiv, Lviv/Galicia, Odesa, Kharkiv, Donetsk, Luhansk), Zakarpattia and Dnipro/Zaporizhzhia assessed and kept, Crimea isolated for its distinct 2014 occupation timeline, and the former nine-oblast 'Central Ukraine (Podillia-Poltava)' catch-all - previously flagged as the zone's weakest inclusion-test case - dissolved into three historic-land regions: Cossack Hetmanate (Poltava UA92 + Cherkasy UA93 + Chernihiv UAA1), Podillia (Vinnytsia UA51 + Khmelnytskyi UA53) and Volhynia-Polissia (Volyn UA81 + Rivne UA83 + Zhytomyr UA82). Kirovohrad (UA91) is re-homed to ua-dnipro-zaporizhzhia: its history is Zaporozhian free-steppe frontier rather than Hetmanate regimental territory, and its economic gravity (Kryvyi Rih basin) points south-east; grouping it with Poltava/Cherkasy would have repeated the SR2024 statistical convenience this split exists to correct.

This design produces 20 zone8 regions (12 Ukrainian + Moldova + Georgia + Armenia + Andorra + Monaco + San Marino + Vatican City + East Thrace), up from 16 in v0.1.0. The growth is a direct consequence of draft-v0.1.2 mandates: the central-catch-all dissolution (+2 net), the Armenia scope amendment (+1) and the East Thrace landmass mandate (+1). Per the region-count tension-flagging principle this is disclosed, not truncated; the representation layer (data/groupings/zone58.json) re-compresses these units into 8 zone8 groupings.

Population figures for Donetsk, Luhansk, and Crimea are pre-war/pre-occupation ceilings (2021 and 2014 Ukrainian state statistics respectively): active occupation, war damage, and mass displacement since 2014/2022 make current, verifiable population counts for these three regions unavailable from Ukrainian government sources, and occupying/de-facto authorities' figures are not treated as reliable census data. Autarky scores for occupied and front-line regions (Donetsk, Luhansk, Crimea, and the occupied portions of Kherson/Zaporizhzhia within ua-odesa-south and ua-dnipro-zaporizhzhia) reflect substantial war-driven degradation relative to pre-war baselines and carry higher uncertainty than the zone's other regions.

Moldova and Georgia are each modelled as single CNTR-geometry regions with empty conflict_flags.zone_nuts_codes for their Transnistria and Abkhazia/South-Ossetia flags respectively: the CNTR country-polygon geometry source provides no sub-national subdivision to map these breakaway territories separately, so per the validation rule that non-empty zone_nuts_codes must resolve to real geometry, these flags carry their full substantive description in the 'description' field with an empty zone_nuts_codes list, which the build pipeline correctly and silently skips from conflicts.geojson - an accepted data limitation rather than an error.

CRITICAL BLOCKER (flagged, not silently worked around): the committed pipeline/raw/NUTS_RG_20M_2024_4326.geojson contains exactly ONE feature for Ukraine - a single country-level polygon with NUTS_ID='UA' (LEVL_CODE 0) - and none of the 177 SR2024 oblast/district codes listed in data/nuts_index.json (sourced from the xlsx in Task 1) have corresponding sub-national geometry in that file. This means every ua-* region's nuts_codes in this file (all SR2024 codes at level 2) will fail check_codes_resolve/validate_all, even though the schema, content, cross-record, and CNTR-based checks all pass. This is a Task 2 (geometry-fetch) / pipeline-raw-data gap, not a defect in this file's authored content: Eurostat's GISCO NUTS_RG product evidently ships Ukraine only as a candidate-country outline, not with the SR2024 statistical-region breakdown the brief assumed was 'verified reachable' in that same file. See zone8-report.md for the exact failing test names and a recommended fix (source real Ukraine oblast boundary geometry, e.g. an admin-1 GeoJSON keyed to SR2024 NUTS_ID-compatible codes, into pipeline/raw/, or fall back to a single undivided 'UA' region with the mandated splits documented as deferred-pending-geometry).

Five zone8 conflict_flags (zakarpattia-minority-identity, kherson-frontline-occupation, donetsk-occupation-frontline, luhansk-occupation-status, zaporizhzhia-npp-and-frontline) were originally authored with sub-oblast (raion/district-level) zone_nuts_codes (e.g. UA213, UA432) to pinpoint occupied or minority-concentration areas more precisely than the oblast as a whole. Task 4 geometry integration resolves Ukraine only at the oblast (ADM1) level via geoBoundaries -- no raion-level geometry is available in this pipeline -- so those five flags' zone_nuts_codes were cleared to [] per the same accepted-limitation precedent already documented above for Moldova/Georgia's Transnistria and Abkhazia/South-Ossetia flags: their full substantive description is retained, and the validation rule that non-empty zone_nuts_codes must resolve to real geometry means the build pipeline correctly and silently skips them from conflicts.geojson rather than failing or misrepresenting the affected area as the entire oblast. crimea-occupation-status is unaffected (UA44/UA45 are oblast-level codes that already resolve).

Schema v2 migration (draft-v0.1.2): variant_group/variant_role removed; default_visible, special_status, pole (with central_coord per amendment A1), reach, parliament, lang_family and autarky.rationales (water/food/energy) added to every record. All four microstates carry mandated special_status values (Vatican 'sovereign enclave', San Marino 'enclave microstate', Monaco 'sovereign city-state microstate', Andorra 'co-principality microstate') rendered with dashed strokes. Ukrainian units carry parliament.has_own=false with the oblast-council note: oblasna rada are local self-government organs under the unitary constitution, not regional parliaments.

Armenia (am-armenia) is added per controller amendment A1 as a single-unit sovereign state with CNTR geometry (CNTR_ID 'AM'), following the Moldova/Georgia precedent, with a Nagorno-Karabakh displacement conflict_flag (text-only, empty zone_nuts_codes, per the MD/GE precedent for CNTR-geometry states).

East Thrace (tr-east-thrace, NUTS2024 TR21) is included solely for European-landmass completeness per the draft-v0.1.2 coverage mandate: Turkey remains excluded as a whole, Istanbul province (TR10) is excluded with it even though partly European, and the unit carries a special_status dashed stroke plus an Istanbul reach note to keep its exceptional basis visible on the map itself.
